jobs.title: Senior Director, Software Engineering - Contract Intelligence
jobs.text:
As the most trusted global leader in data-first contract lifecycle management (CLM) software, Agiloft helps organizations manage the end-to-end process of proposing, negotiating, signing, and leveraging contracts using our flexible Data-first Agreement Platform (DAP). With contract data as the foundation, customers quickly and collaboratively reach agreement and leverage contract visibility to thrive with competitive advantage. Employing powerful, pragmatic artificial intelligence as a legal force multiplier, and robust integration capabilities as a data liberator, organizations around the world trust Agiloft’s certified implementers to deliver connected, intelligent, and autonomous solutions across the entire contract lifecycle.
Top analysts like Gartner, Forrester, and IDC agree, all showing Agiloft as a leader in the CLM space. Our no code platform is easily managed and administered by business users, which is why Agiloft is the contract you keep: nearly a full 100% of new customers are satisfied with their initial implementations, and some 97% of customers renew every year. Ours is a growing, vibrant, successful company that is at the forefront of a market that is becoming a must-have for all organizations.
We believe that the way to build the strongest, most vibrant place to work is to bring in individuals from all walks of life, and to support them in bringing their authentic selves to their day, every day. Our working philosophy is that “EX = CX”: when employee experience is excellent, so is customer experience. We support multiple Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), and offer a working environment that supports healthy work/life balance, including floating holidays and a quarterly, no-questions-asked wellness day.
Position Overview
AI is changing CLM, and Agiloft is building what comes next. As Senior Director, Software Engineering - Contract Intelligence, you will lead the engineering teams behind Astra Agents and the Contract Intelligence Graph (CIG). These are the capabilities that turn contracts into intelligence customers act on every day. You will own engineering strategy, organization, and execution across this portfolio, together with the shared platform components and interfaces that serve these experiences.
This is a rare chance to shape and build a converged platform that makes these products work as one and that future Agiloft experiences will build on. The shared platform scope includes common data models and database services, identity and access management (IAM), agent and AI Assistant capabilities, and a unified interface suite spanning APIs, user interfaces, and MCP servers. You will decide how each product consumes these capabilities while preserving the flexibility each experience needs.
Reporting directly to the CTO and working closely with Product, Design, Applied AI & Knowledge Engineering, Core CLM Engineering, and Cloud Operations, you will turn ambitious product priorities into an integrated technical roadmap and dependable delivery that drives measurable customer value.
You will lead managers, technical leaders, and distributed teams. This role is for a leader who stays close to the code, holds a high bar, and builds a culture where strong engineers do their best work.
Success means shared capabilities are adopted across Astra and CLM, the architecture remains secure and scalable, releases are predictable, and the organization can deliver customer value without sacrificing quality, reliability, or long-term maintainability. If you want to shape how enterprises manage their contracts in the AI era, and build the team that makes it happen, we’d love to talk with you.
Job Responsibilities
Contract Intelligence Strategy & Outcomes
Own engineering outcomes across Astra and the CLM cloud-native services for Agents and CIG, including the APIs, integrations, and orchestration capabilities that support them.
Partner with Product and Design leadership to shape strategy, roadmap, sequencing, and investment decisions, using customer feedback and adoption signals to guide priorities.
Translate portfolio priorities into integrated engineering plans, technical investments, clear ownership, and explicit cross-team dependencies.
Define and review measures of customer impact, adoption, business value, delivery predictability, and product quality.
Converged Platform Architecture & Interfaces
Define architecture direction and a convergence roadmap for shared data models, database services, IAM, Agents, and AI Assistants serving Astra and CLM cloud-native services for Agents and CIG.
Design shared components so they can be consumed consistently across Astra and CLM while allowing product-specific extensions where needed; establish clear service boundaries and ownership across Astra, Agents, CIG, and Core CLM.
Own a unified interface suite across APIs, user interfaces, and MCP servers, with consistent contracts and patterns for Astra and CLM cloud-native Agent and CIG services.
Guide cloud-native APIs and integrations, including MCP and other AI orchestration interfaces for Contract Intelligence workflows and customer systems; ensure services are secure, tenant-aware, scalable, observable, versioned, reliable, and backward compatible.
Improve API, UI, and MCP design standards, documentation, and developer experience for Agiloft teams, customers, and partners.
Agents, AI Assistants & Contract Intelligence Graph
Partner with Applied AI & Knowledge Engineering to translate AI and knowledge capabilities into production-ready Agents and AI Assistants, service interfaces, architecture, and engineering plans.
Establish practices for evaluating AI-enabled features, including output quality, permissions, privacy, latency, cost, and operational behavior.
Guide engineering evolution of CIG and the services used by Agents and AI Assistants so they provide a dependable foundation for Contract Intelligence experiences across Astra and CLM.
Set appropriate technical guardrails for AI-powered workflows and integrations with external systems.
Delivery Excellence & Operational Reliability
Own the software development lifecycle across the Contract Intelligence engineering organization, including planning, development, testing, release coordination, and post-release stabilization.
Coordinate dependencies and release plans across Astra, CLM cloud-native services, Core CLM, and other integration teams.
Establish operational measures such as service availability, API latency, error rates, integration reliability, and incident recurrence; use them to drive improvement.
Lead root-cause analysis and remediation for significant incidents and Level 3 technical escalations within the domain.
Balance roadmap delivery with reliability, security, modernization, performance, and long-term technical health.
Be a hands-on technical contributor to the codebase, code reviews, and architecture decisions.
Organization, Talent & Cross-functional Leadership
Lead managers and technical leaders responsible for Astra, Agents, CIG, and the supporting integration capabilities.
Align Astra team priorities and technical direction with shared components and CLM cloud-native services while maintaining clear accountability for each product outcome.
Develop managers and senior engineers through clear expectations, coaching, delegation, feedback, performance management, and career development.
Build an accountable, collaborative engineering culture with strong technical ownership, predictable execution, and continuous learning across distributed teams.
Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain strong engineering talent; identify capability, capacity, and organizational needs as the portfolio grows.
Partner across Product, Design, Core CLM, Applied AI & Knowledge Engineering, QA, Cloud Operations, Security, and Support to resolve dependencies and deliver customer outcomes.
Communicate technical direction, tradeoffs, delivery risks, and investment needs clearly; serve as an engineering escalation point for complex Contract Intelligence issues.
Other duties as assigned.
Required Qualifications
BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including 5+ years leading and developing multi-team engineering organizations with managers and senior technical leaders with clear delivery accountability and performance management.
Demonstrated ownership of engineering outcomes for a substantial product portfolio, platform, or technical domain, measured by customer adoption, usage, and business value.
Deep experience with cloud-based SaaS systems, distributed services, APIs, enterprise integrations, and user-facing applications, with sufficient technical fluency to guide architecture and evaluate tradeoffs.
Demonstrated success building shared or converged components used by multiple products or services, including data models, database services, and IAM, with clear interfaces and ownership boundaries.
Hands-on technical fluency in production AI/LLM functionality, Agents, and AI Assistants, including the engineering practices needed to assess quality, privacy, reliability, and cost.
Strong understanding of engineering measures such as delivery predictability, service reliability and SLOs, defect trends, performance, and operational health.
Proven partnership with Product and Design to turn customer priorities into executable engineering roadmaps, including sound build, buy or partner decisions, and to deliver predictability against reliability and quality measure.
Clear communicator who translates technical risks, tradeoffs and decisions into business terms for executives and cross-functional partners.
Sound responsible AI judgement, with experience setting guardrails for accuracy, privacy, security, permissions, transparency and human oversight in customer-facing AI features.
Develops managers and technical leaders, builds succession and helps people do their best work.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience leading AI-enabled products, Agent architectures, or orchestration interfaces such as MCP.
Experience with knowledge graphs, graph-based systems, or other data-rich enterprise platforms.
Background in CLM, legal technology, workflow automation, or enterprise SaaS.
Experience scaling engineering organizations and operating practices as products grow, including in compliance-driven environments.
Ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace is our priority. We are committed to an environment of acceptance where you are free to bring your full self to work. All employment decisions at Agiloft are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications without regard to race, color, religion or belief, national or social ethnic origin, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, parental status, marital status, Veteran status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. If you have a need that requires accommodation during the recruiting process, please let us know by contacting Director, Talent Acquisition, Brad Toothman at .
Applicants from underrepresented groups such as minorities, veterans, or individuals with disabilities encouraged to apply.
Applications will be reviewed as submitted. There will be no application deadline for this opportunity.

jobs.title: Head of Forward Deployed Engineering
jobs.text:
Build AI products people use—and lead the engineers who ship them
Single Grain is hiring a technical player-coach to lead six engineers, build alongside them, and turn customer problems into secure, reliable products that hit their engagement goals.
You should be deeply hands-on with AI: we expect 95%+ of your code to be written with AI, with you accountable for architecture, verification, useful reviews and production quality. You need to know what to build, what to prioritize and what to stop.
About Single Grain
Single Grain combines marketing services, software and AI to drive measurable customer results. This role connects engineering work to that larger vision. You will help the team turn useful discoveries into products clients adopt, maintain and expand.
What you will own
Manage six engineers. Set assignments, sequence work, manage capacity, coach people and make ownership clear.
Build alongside the team. Own technical standards, architecture, technical and PR reviews, and release readiness.
Talk to customers regularly. Discover the real problem, test assumptions, set success metrics and use adoption data to decide what to improve or kill.
Drive engagement within products. Own rollout, activation, repeat use and recovery when a product misses its goals.
Ship at pace with careful execution. Test failure paths, challenge weak assumptions and make PR feedback useful. Do not ship poor-quality work simply to increase output.
Govern security and AI costs: access and data boundaries, tests/evals, token attribution, budgets, alerts, context and retry limits, monitoring and recovery.
Connect each project to the company vision and measurable customer value. Scope useful follow-on work with clients and partner with account owners on expansion.
Build reusable components and delivery playbooks that engineers actually use.
What success looks like
By day 30: agree the delivery priorities, the first four systems, product engagement targets and a clear operating rhythm with Eric and customer owners.
By day 60: put technical review, security, AI-cost controls and release checks into regular use.
By day 90: deliver four distinct production systems used by real users, with acceptance, instrumentation, support ownership and recovery plans. Demos and artificially split features do not count.
Product success: hit agreed engagement targets within a measurement window suited to each product. Review misses and recovery actions weekly.
By day 120: all six engineers independently own bounded delivery from discovery through launch and measurement, with peer review and escalation intact.
Each month: produce one useful reusable component or playbook; reach 12 by day 365. Unused documentation does not count.
Evidence we want to see
Comparable experience managing engineers while staying technically credible and actively building.
Production systems you helped ship and operate, with measurable customer adoption or business outcomes and a clear account of your contribution.
A history of promotions and increasing responsibility, supported by sustained results. Equivalent growth in scope matters too.
Daily AI-assisted engineering and management workflows. Be ready to explain how you create, test, review and maintain AI-written code.
Strong organization, attention to detail, customer development, product judgment and clear communication.
Examples of decisions to focus, narrow scope or stop work, and how those decisions served a larger goal.
How the process works
Application and evidence review, our standard five-question AI prescreen for selected candidates, a live discussion and proof exercise based on your own work, a small paid exercise where substantial work is required, and references. Safe redacted or recreated examples are welcome for confidential work.
Work model and compensation
Full-time and remote. Being based in Los Angeles is a strong plus, not a requirement. Annual compensation is $175,000–$225,000 USD, based on experience and qualifications.
Benefits
Single Grain's published benefits include medical, dental and vision insurance; life insurance; a 401(k) with a 4% match; unlimited PTO; monthly UberEats; a MacBook; and a home-office stipend/setup. Benefits are subject to applicable plan terms and eligibility.
Apply
Apply through this job's application form with your resume or professional profile. We will send the standard AI prescreen separately to selected candidates.

jobs.title: VP & GM: Product Platform
jobs.text:
Why Entersekt
Founded over 16 years ago, with more recent investments from Accel-KKR, Entersekt is a leader in digital banking fraud prevention and payment security, including mobile authentication, mobile app security, and 3D Secure authentication for issuers, acquirers and payment networks. We offer highly scalable products with a track record of success across multiple continents.
Entersekt enables secure digital transactions for leading financial institutions globally. We exist to create a world where everyone can transact digitally without fear or compromise. Currently, we protect the digital transactions of over 210 million active users on our platform and hold 120 active patents that recognize innovation in digital security, payments, and user experience. Entersekt offers customers secure authentication and digital payments experiences that remove unnecessary friction. Entersekt has a diverse product portfolio and aggressive roadmap that positions the company well to sustain competitive advantage as it expands globally with emphasis on North America and European markets.
The Ideal Candidate
We are looking for a strategic and commercially minded product leader who combines strong platform thinking with a relentless focus on adoption and business value. Accountable not just for the health of the platform components individually, but for the penetration and value they deliver when embedded across the broader portfolio. Own the strategy, roadmap, and business performance for the Entersekt Platform including Portal, Administration, Reporting, Detection & Decisioning capabilities.

Experience defining and managing product health and performance measures covering areas such as adoption, usage, reliability, performance and stakeholder/customer satisfaction.
Proven experience partnering closely with Engineering and technical leadership on architecture, integration, technical debt and platform scalability decisions.

jobs.title: Vice President, Product
jobs.text:
*CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES**
About SafelyYou
SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.
Originating in 2015 as the doctoral research of CEO George Netscher—and inspired by his own family's experience with Alzheimer's disease—SafelyYou was spun out of UC Berkeley’s Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, one of the top five AI research groups in the world. And today, our company is solving critical challenges in senior living, from resident falls and ER visits to staffing concerns, length of stay, and NOI. All helping ensure that communities can focus on improved care for residents while still reaching their financial goals.
SafelyYou is one of five most innovative fall technologies referenced in the Senate Falls Report (2019), a winner of the McKnight’s Tech Partner of the Year, and has been named to Fortune’s Impact 20 list, which recognizes companies making people’s lives better through innovation.
Your Role at SafelyYou
Our product works; how we build hasn't kept up. Our product and technology teams own customer outcomes, built on shared platforms. As VP of Product, you lead the product management team and own the portfolio: one committed roadmap, where investment goes, and which bets get funded, changed, or stopped. The CPTO sets overall direction and the VP of Engineering owns delivery; you own product execution You'll inherit a capable team ready for a stronger operating model, and part of the job is deciding what to keep, rebuild, and stop. Operators are choosing their technology partners for the next decade, and you'll have a seat at the leadership table as we earn that choice. Every improvement you ship reaches residents, families, and caregivers. You'll work daily with the CPTO and VP of Engineering, and closely with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, our clinical team, Operations, and Strategy.
Key Responsibilities:
The Numbers You'll Own
Customer NOI. Own SafelyYou's impact on operator NOI per resident, proven with outcome data in each care setting.
Wellness AI and staffing intelligence. Build both into scaled product lines alongside Safety AI.
Throughput. Double the rate of committed features launched to customers within the next year, measured by release to market and adoption, not tickets closed.
What You'll Own
One roadmap. A single customer-facing roadmap tied to company objectives. Sales sells what's committed.
The portfolio. Allocate investment across customer-facing teams, shared platforms (AI, data and integrations, devices, hardware), and longer-horizon bets, and make stage-gate calls on evidence.
The operating model.With the VP of Engineering, run annual strategy, quarterly planning, and published decision rights. Build the operations support PMs need to focus on outcomes.
The ecosystem. Drive partner adoption so SafelyYou insights reach caregivers inside the EHR and eCall systems they already use.
Trusted AI. Clear accuracy and false-alarm standards, privacy by design, and evidence before anything reaches the field.
The market. Be in the room with our largest operators, shape pricing and packaging with Sales and Marketing, and represent product at industry events and with investors.
The team. Coach, level, and hire product managers, and build a bench of future leaders.
The Ideal Candidate:
The hard requirement:you've led product managers through an operating-model change, such as functional teams to outcome and platform teams, on products that combine hardware, AI/ML, and cloud software.
10+ years in product, including 5+ years leading PMs across multiple product areas.
AI/ML, hardware, and platform or partner-ecosystem products shipped to market, including stage-gated development, certification, and field reliability.
Enterprise B2B credibility. You've carried a product number, not just supported one.
A decisive player-coach and clear writer who earns engineering's respect.
Strongly preferred, and learnable:healthcare or senior living experience, and regulated products (HIPAA, life-safety).
Salary Range:$260,000 - $280,000 USD commensurate with experience
Why Join Us? You Can Make a Difference!
SafelyYou offers a competitive compensation package, including but not limited to:
A mission-driven company culture
Fully remote
Competitive salary & benefits, including fully paid employee premiums for Medical, Dental, and Vision
401k Program
Monthly Education, Well-being & WFH stipends
Non-accrual PTO
Growth Potential
Company Retreats
Medical & Family/Parental Leave
At SafelyYou, we believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace makes us a more relevant, competitive, and resilient company. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workforce that celebrates diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.
We value all the perspectives our team members bring to the table, and that is why we don’t look for culture fit, but culture add. We want to hear from YOU! We encourage you to apply even if you do not fit 100% of the technical requirements.

jobs.title: Director, Software Engineering
jobs.text:
About Feanix Bio
Feanix is rebuilding animal breeding from the genome up.
We’re a YC-backed startup using whole-genome sequencing and custom ML models to help dairy farmers make better breeding and herd management decisions. Our technology is genuinely novel: we can sequence a full genome from a single hair at a fraction of traditional industry costs, our models achieve ~90% prediction accuracy on traits where existing approaches sit closer to ~30%, and we’re pioneering farm-specific genomic predictions that turn genetics into practical, actionable decisions.
That technology is translating into real adoption. In a short time, we’ve grown to serve roughly 1% of the U.S. dairy industry, with many customers in the pipeline. We started with dairy because our founders grew up on dairy farms and understand firsthand the problems we’re solving. But genetics is foundational to every agricultural industry, and dairy is only the beginning.
We’re building Feanix with a small, high-caliber team where people have meaningful ownership and work end to end. There are no unnecessary layers and very little room for busywork — just difficult problems at the intersection of biology, data, and software that haven’t been solved before.
If you’re exceptional at what you do and want your work to have a measurable impact on an entire industry, we’d love to build it with you.
About The Role
Feanix is expanding its product offerings based on our farmers' needs and moving into other species, and engineering has to scale with these business goals. Today we're a small, tight engineering team behind one core product: Autopilot and sire mating, the decision engine farmers act on every day. We're shifting from individuals carrying whole systems to teams that share them, and we're growing in close partnership with our product organization. Over the next 12–18 months we plan to grow engineering to around 30 people. The technology organization includes software, hardware, and product, and this role leads software development.
You'll be our first Director of Engineering, reporting to the CTO. You'll lead a team of engineering managers: two have already joined, and you'll hire more to support the organization's growth. Our staff and principal engineers, who lead architecture, also report directly to you rather than to the EMs. You run the engineering org and its delivery, and you set technical direction together with them.
You'll report to a repeat CTO who wants thought partners: people who lay out the options, show their reasoning, and ask what we'd do if the current options disappeared. You'll also be one of a small group of technical leaders setting direction for the company. We're growing fast and working with biological systems, so designing with an experimental mindset is crucial.. You should be comfortable with ambiguity and making good calls with incomplete information.
The impact of this role is through your people. Your output is a team that ships: clear roles, managers who can build and run teams of 6–8 engineers, and cohesive system and team design. We expect you to be technically credible and fluent in how software is now built, but you won't be writing production code or doing line-by-line review.
Your Partnership With Product and Hardware
You'll join the growing director team in our technology organization, alongside our Director of Product and Director of Hardware. Together you'll deliver products with one goal: making farms as profitable and efficient as possible. We do that through the best possible breeding decisions for cattle, sensors that collect phenotypic data, and analysis built on the genomic data we collect and process.
As a team, you're accountable for keeping our existing products stable and growing their value, while prototyping, testing, and rolling out new ones.
What You'll Do
Lead and support the engineering managers. Our EMs are experienced managers, and your job is to make them more effective. Give them the context, support, and clear expectations they need to build high-functioning teams with real accountability for outcomes. Unblock them across teams, back their hard calls, and hold them to a consistent bar. Hire the managers we'll need as we grow.
Design the org as it grows. In partnership with the CTO and your fellow directors, grow the engineering organization. Gather signals and input from engineers, EMs, and the teams closest to farmers, and use them to turn high-level plans into a concrete org and roadmap that meet customer needs. Decide when and how teams split, and draw boundaries around the architecture rather than around labels. Our working areas are platform and decision engine, farm delivery (data on and off farm computers, automation, QC), modeling and genomics, and new planned product lines.
Build how we hire and onboard. With the CTO and our recruiting team, create and refine an engineering hiring process that attracts high-quality talent and keeps the bar high as we grow. Make sure new engineers onboard quickly, and that people are in the right seats as teams form and change.
Make delivery predictable. With the Director of Product, turn strategy into committed outcomes for each team. Surface tradeoffs early, and report progress in terms of what reached farms, not activity.
Protect platform investment. Make sure the infrastructure that unlocks future products is designed, staffed, and built alongside customer work. Make platform and architecture calls together with the CTO and your architecture leaders.
Lead an AI-native engineering org. Our engineers work spec-first and direct coding agents. Set the standards (specs, evals, testing, CI, and security) that let people and agents ship safely without heavy process. Decide where agents should carry the load, such as support and bug fixing, and where people need to. When agent output goes wrong, fix the spec or harness, not just the symptom, and keep evolving these practices as the tools change.
Build the operating system. Put in place the lightweight rhythm a fast team actually uses: escalation paths, incident response, release discipline, and knowing who's responsible for what.
Shape how we plan and grow people. With the CTO and your fellow directors, help build the leveling framework for technical roles, our planning cycles, and our performance review system, so expectations are clear and growth paths are fair for both managers and ICs.
Partner across Feanix. Work with Farm Success, Farm Ops, and our science teams so what we ship holds up on real farms. Join farm visits and stay close to the customer.
What Success Looks Like
First 30 days: You understand your peers across the organization and how engineering works with each of them. You've started setting expectations with your direct reports. You've reviewed our technical hiring process and made improvements where it needs them. You've spent time on a farm and know the system and the customer.
First 90 days: Technical hiring is operationalized: you've built on the process we already have, not redesigned it, and it runs reliably with the EMs and recruiting. You and the Director of Product have aligned on the roadmap, and you're confident it's achievable with the team we have and the team we're hiring; where it isn't, the tradeoffs are on the table. You've established a working partnership with the Director of Hardware and agreed on how hardware and software teams will plan and hand off work. Your EMs know what you expect of them, and each team has clear goals and a delivery cadence you can report on.
First 6 months: At least one new product has launched to farms, our hardware pilots have the software they need, and the core product has stayed stable as we've grown.
First 12 months: Engineering has supported the company's sales and impact goals for the year: farms are onboarded as fast as we sign them, new products reach farms on schedule, and the organization is ready to take on what comes next.
What You Bring
10+ years in software engineering, including 5+ years managing engineers and at least 2 years managing managers. You reached a senior engineering level as an IC first.
A track record of scaling an engineering org at a startup through a growth phase, ideally from around 10 to 30+ engineers, including splitting teams and adding a management layer as you went.
Managers you can point to: people you hired or promoted into management and developed into strong leaders.
Experience building engineering hiring processes that attract strong talent, including calibrating interviewers and closing senior candidates.
Experience leading delivery across several products or teams at once, and balancing customer-facing roadmap work against platform and infrastructure investment.
Deep fluency with AI-native engineering. You've moved teams to spec-first, agentic development, and you have real opinions on specs, evals, verification, and quality in that world. You use AI daily in your own leadership work.
A strong partnership record with product leaders: you've worked as an equal partner to a head of product, not as an order-taker or a gatekeeper.
Experience partnering with hardware or science leaders to deliver products that span physical devices, data, and software.
Clear written communication and the judgment to report status, risk, and tradeoffs at the right level for the CTO, CEO, and board.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience leading teams that ship ML, data-intensive, or decision-support products
Experience with platform re-architecture while the business kept shipping: data models, pipelines, or event-driven systems
Experience with products that combine software with hardware, sensors, or edge compute
Experience in a remote-first engineering org
Interest in agriculture, biology, genomics, or working close to a physical industry
Ultimately, we care far more about demonstrated ability, curiosity, and problem-solving than pedigree or conventional career paths.
Logistics
Remote (US), ideally able to work west coast hours
Travel about 20% of the time: recruiting, time with teams and at our headquarters, and customer farm visits
Why You'll Enjoy Working With Us
The People - we have an amazing group of talented, smart and fun people on our team!
The Company - we are building something novel that has not been done before which is making a huge impact on the dairy industry!
The Experience - you get to come in and be a part of ground breaking work that will have a huge impact on generations to come!
Compensation and Benefits
Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship or transfers at this time.
Actual starting pay for this role is determined by a variety of factors including but not limited to qualifications, experience, relevant skills, education, and geographic location. Employees are offered a variety of benefits to empower them with the resources and flexibility they need to enjoy success on the job and to live a healthy life.
We offer a flexible, remote-friendly work environment for most roles, along with a growing benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401k, pet insurance, flexible paid time off; and paid parental leave, including up to twelve weeks of paid leave and/or supplemental pay coordination with applicable state benefits.
Pay Transparency
$200,000—$230,000 USD
Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship or transfers at this time.
Compensation is based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and location. Benefits include equity options, medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k); flexible PTO; paid parental leave; and pet insurance.
Feanix Biotechnologies is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on any characteristic protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available throughout the application and interview process.
By applying, you consent to Feanix Biotechnologies processing your personal information for recruitment purposes in accordance with applicable privacy laws.

We started with dairy because our founders grew up on dairy farms and understand firsthand the problems we’re solving. But genetics is foundational to every agricultural industry, and dairy is only the beginning.

We’re building Feanix with a small, high-caliber team where people have meaningful ownership and work end to end. There are no unnecessary layers and very little room for busywork — just difficult problems at the intersection of biology, data, and software that haven’t been solved before.
If you’re exceptional at what you do and want your work to have a measurable impact on an entire industry, we’d love to build it with you.
About The Role

Feanix is expanding its product offerings based on our farmers' needs and moving into other species, and engineering has to scale with these business goals. Today we're a small, tight engineering team behind one core product: Autopilot and sire mating, the decision engine farmers act on every day. We're shifting from individuals carrying whole systems to teams that share them, and we're growing in close partnership with our product organization. Over the next 12–18 months we plan to grow engineering to around 30 people. The technology organization includes software, hardware, and product, and this role leads software development.

You'll be our first Director of Engineering, reporting to the CTO. You'll lead a team of engineering managers: two have already joined, and you'll hire more to support the organization's growth. Our staff and principal engineers, who lead architecture, also report directly to you rather than to the EMs. You run the engineering org and its delivery, and you set technical direction together with them.

You'll report to a repeat CTO who wants thought partners: people who lay out the options, show their reasoning, and ask what we'd do if the current options disappeared. You'll also be one of a small group of technical leaders setting direction for the company. We're growing fast and working with biological systems, so designing with an experimental mindset is crucial.. You should be comfortable with ambiguity and making good calls with incomplete information.

The impact of this role is through your people. Your output is a team that ships: clear roles, managers who can build and run teams of 6–8 engineers, and cohesive system and team design. We expect you to be technically credible and fluent in how software is now built, but you won't be writing production code or doing line-by-line review.
Your Partnership With Product and Hardware

You'll join the growing director team in our technology organization, alongside our Director of Product and Director of Hardware. Together you'll deliver products with one goal: making farms as profitable and efficient as possible. We do that through the best possible breeding decisions for cattle, sensors that collect phenotypic data, and analysis built on the genomic data we collect and process.
As a team, you're accountable for keeping our existing products stable and growing their value, while prototyping, testing, and rolling out new ones.
What You'll Do

items: Lead and support the engineering managers. Our EMs are experienced managers, and your job is to make them more effective. Give them the context, support, and clear expectations they need to build high-functioning teams with real accountability for outcomes. Unblock them across teams, back their hard calls, and hold them to a consistent bar. Hire the managers we'll need as we grow.

Design the org as it grows. In partnership with the CTO and your fellow directors, grow the engineering organization. Gather signals and input from engineers, EMs, and the teams closest to farmers, and use them to turn high-level plans into a concrete org and roadmap that meet customer needs. Decide when and how teams split, and draw boundaries around the architecture rather than around labels. Our working areas are platform and decision engine, farm delivery (data on and off farm computers, automation, QC), modeling and genomics, and new planned product lines.

Build how we hire and onboard. With the CTO and our recruiting team, create and refine an engineering hiring process that attracts high-quality talent and keeps the bar high as we grow. Make sure new engineers onboard quickly, and that people are in the right seats as teams form and change.

Make delivery predictable. With the Director of Product, turn strategy into committed outcomes for each team. Surface tradeoffs early, and report progress in terms of what reached farms, not activity.

Protect platform investment. Make sure the infrastructure that unlocks future products is designed, staffed, and built alongside customer work. Make platform and architecture calls together with the CTO and your architecture leaders.

Lead an AI-native engineering org. Our engineers work spec-first and direct coding agents. Set the standards (specs, evals, testing, CI, and security) that let people and agents ship safely without heavy process. Decide where agents should carry the load, such as support and bug fixing, and where people need to. When agent output goes wrong, fix the spec or harness, not just the symptom, and keep evolving these practices as the tools change.
Build the operating system. Put in place the lightweight rhythm a fast team actually uses: escalation paths, incident response, release discipline, and knowing who's responsible for what.

Shape how we plan and grow people. With the CTO and your fellow directors, help build the leveling framework for technical roles, our planning cycles, and our performance review system, so expectations are clear and growth paths are fair for both managers and ICs.
Partner across Feanix. Work with Farm Success, Farm Ops, and our science teams so what we ship holds up on real farms. Join farm visits and stay close to the customer.

blocks.text: What Success Looks Like

items: First 30 days: You understand your peers across the organization and how engineering works with each of them. You've started setting expectations with your direct reports. You've reviewed our technical hiring process and made improvements where it needs them. You've spent time on a farm and know the system and the customer.

First 90 days: Technical hiring is operationalized: you've built on the process we already have, not redesigned it, and it runs reliably with the EMs and recruiting. You and the Director of Product have aligned on the roadmap, and you're confident it's achievable with the team we have and the team we're hiring; where it isn't, the tradeoffs are on the table. You've established a working partnership with the Director of Hardware and agreed on how hardware and software teams will plan and hand off work. Your EMs know what you expect of them, and each team has clear goals and a delivery cadence you can report on.
First 6 months: At least one new product has launched to farms, our hardware pilots have the software they need, and the core product has stayed stable as we've grown.

First 12 months: Engineering has supported the company's sales and impact goals for the year: farms are onboarded as fast as we sign them, new products reach farms on schedule, and the organization is ready to take on what comes next.

blocks.text: What You Bring

items: 10+ years in software engineering, including 5+ years managing engineers and at least 2 years managing managers. You reached a senior engineering level as an IC first.
A track record of scaling an engineering org at a startup through a growth phase, ideally from around 10 to 30+ engineers, including splitting teams and adding a management layer as you went.
Managers you can point to: people you hired or promoted into management and developed into strong leaders.
Experience building engineering hiring processes that attract strong talent, including calibrating interviewers and closing senior candidates.
Experience leading delivery across several products or teams at once, and balancing customer-facing roadmap work against platform and infrastructure investment.

Deep fluency with AI-native engineering. You've moved teams to spec-first, agentic development, and you have real opinions on specs, evals, verification, and quality in that world. You use AI daily in your own leadership work.
A strong partnership record with product leaders: you've worked as an equal partner to a head of product, not as an order-taker or a gatekeeper.
Experience partnering with hardware or science leaders to deliver products that span physical devices, data, and software.
Clear written communication and the judgment to report status, risk, and tradeoffs at the right level for the CTO, CEO, and board.

blocks.text: Preferred Qualifications

items: Experience leading teams that ship ML, data-intensive, or decision-support products
Experience with platform re-architecture while the business kept shipping: data models, pipelines, or event-driven systems
Experience with products that combine software with hardware, sensors, or edge compute
Experience in a remote-first engineering org
Interest in agriculture, biology, genomics, or working close to a physical industry

blocks.text: Ultimately, we care far more about demonstrated ability, curiosity, and problem-solving than pedigree or conventional career paths.

items: Remote (US), ideally able to work west coast hours
Travel about 20% of the time: recruiting, time with teams and at our headquarters, and customer farm visits

blocks.text: Why You'll Enjoy Working With Us

items: The People - we have an amazing group of talented, smart and fun people on our team!

jobs.title: Director of Product Management, Secure File Gateway and ICAP
jobs.text:
OPSWAT, a global leader in IT, OT, and ICS critical infrastructure cybersecurity, delivers an end-to-end platform that gives public and private sector organizations and enterprises the critical advantage needed to protect their complex networks, secure their devices, and ensure compliance. Over the last 20 years our commitment to innovative technology has earned the trust of more than 1,700 organizations, governments, and institutions globally, solidifying our role in protecting the world’s critical infrastructure and securing our way of life.
Why This Role Matters
At OPSWAT, protecting the world’s critical infrastructure is not an abstract mission. It is real, urgent, and growing. Our ICAP product is a proven, high-impact solution that is trusted by customers who depend on us to secure their most critical systems. We are now ready to take ICAP to the next level.
This Director role is a rare opportunity to shape the future of ICAP, including the evolution toward a next-generation Proxy, while scaling commercial impact and deepening customer value. You will operate at the intersection of product strategy, engineering execution, and go-to-market success, with clear ownership and visible impact. If you are energized by building success, driving innovation, and owning outcomes, this role was designed for you.
What You Will Be Doing
As Director of AI Product Management, you will be the end-to-end owner of ICAP’s product strategy and growth trajectory.
You will:
Set and own the ICAP product vision and roadmap, including the strategic evolution into a Proxy-focused solution.
Translate market signals, customer needs, and competitive insights into clear product direction and prioritized investments.
Partner deeply with Engineering, ensuring fast, high-quality execution and scalable architecture.
Work closely with Sales, Sales Engineering, and Marketing to drive bookings, pipeline, and customer adoption.
Serve as a strong, visible product leader across regions, with a close partnership with our Vietnam-based teams.
Balance innovation with operational excellence, ensuring ICAP continues to deliver reliability, performance, and trust at scale.
Represent ICAP with confidence to customers, partners, and internal leadership.
What Success Looks Like
In your first 12–18 months, success will look like:
A clear, compelling ICAP roadmap aligned to market demand and customer value.
Measurable growth in bookings and pipeline tied directly to product strategy.
Strong, trust-based partnerships with Engineering and GTM teams.
Progress toward a Proxy-focused architecture that positions ICAP for long-term growth.
A product organization that moves with urgency, clarity, and accountability.
Who You Are
You are a product leader who blends strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
You bring:
Proven experience leading enterprise or security products at scale.
Deep hands on experience building with AI.
Strong understanding of proxy technologies, ICAP, networking, or adjacent security domains.
A track record of partnering effectively with Engineering to deliver complex products.
Commercial acumen and experience supporting bookings, pipeline, and customer conversations.
Comfort operating in a global, distributed environment, including close collaboration with teams in Vietnam.
Clear, confident communication and the ability to influence across functions.
A mindset rooted in ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement.
Director-level experience is preferred, but we value demonstrated leadership altitude, judgment, and impact above title alone.
Why OPSWAT?
OPSWAT is a fast-growing cybersecurity company with a strong culture of ownership and innovation. We build products that matter, support leaders who take initiative, and invest in those who want to grow.
In this role, you will:
Own a successful, revenue-generating product with a meaningful runway.
Shape the future of ICAP and Proxy innovation.
Work with smart, committed teams across the globe.
Have direct visibility and influence within Product leadership.
If you are looking for a role where your decisions matter, your leadership is visible, and your work protects what matters most, we would love to meet you.
OPSWAT is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to providing an environment where equal employment opportunities are extended to all employees and applicants, free of discrimination and harassment of any type. All employment decisions are based on individual qualifications, job requirements, and business needs without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local laws.
Recruiting Agencies: we do not accept unsolicited resumes from third party agencies for any of our open positions. To submit resumes for our jobs, there must be a recruiting contract approved by our legal team and endorsed by both parties. We are currently not accepting additional 3rd party agencies at this time.

jobs.title: VP of Product
jobs.text:
About Us
Fenix24 is a global leader in breach recovery and pre-breach operational recoverability, redefining cyber resilience with the world's first Recovery Dependency Modeling and Recoverability Intelligence Platform, Argos99. Fenix24's
breach recovery team is the largest in the world and has led more than 500 ransomware recoveries in 96 countries, including 30 of the Fortune 500. Pre-breach operational recoverability is founded on that real-world experience and is powered by Argos99 and our Resiliency Operations Center.
Our recoverability platform is purpose-built by frontline recovery experts and is deployed across hybrid cloud and on-premise environments; delivering measurable improvements in recovery readiness and faster, more confident restoration when ransomware strikes.
About This Position
We are searching for a Vice President of Product to join our Fenix24 team. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will play a pivotal role in the future of our company, providing the overall vision for the Argos99 product roadmap and leading the product management function. You'll define the product, help shape the broader portfolio, and have a strong voice in pricing, go-to-market, and commercial strategy. This role will be critical in shaping not only our products, but our entire organization.
This is an incredible opportunity to build the product from the ground up. You'll do real work from day one alongside engineering, architecture, and UX, and build out the product function as Argos99 grows. You'll guide products from conceptualization through planning and development, bringing the leadership, organizational, and execution skills to carry the product lifecycle from strategy through delivery, in support of the business's long-term plans.
Key Responsibilities
Build and lead the product function from the ground up: establish the team, processes, and the metrics and performance framework that govern how product work is tracked, using a data-driven mindset to identify gaps and drive continuous improvement.
Develop and implement strategic product plans, collaborating with customers, prospects, external partners, and internal teams to grow our business.
Own, create, and maintain all product roadmaps and business cases, along with feature backlogs, timelines, business/functional/user requirements, and design artifacts (use cases, user stories, journey maps, etc.).
Lead evidence-based product definition, User Experience (UX) design, and market, user, and competitive research.
Own pricing strategy and market launch, and coordinate with the sales, support, and services teams.
Lead cross-functionally, bringing engineering, architecture, UX, sales, support, and services together around shared goals, and tell the product story clearly, both internally and externally.
Represent and advocate for the customer and end user through every stage of the product experience: development, delivery, deployment, and adoption.
Other duties as required.
Qualifications, Requirements & Preferred Skills
10+ years in product management, including time as the senior product decision-maker for an early-stage B2B SaaS product.
5+ years of experience in the cybersecurity/infrastructure/resiliency industry, with deep fluency in how enterprise infrastructure is built, run, attacked, and recovered. That fluency could come from cybersecurity, backup and data protection, IT operations, incident response, or hands-on practitioner work.
3+ years of experience with MSP/MSSPs.
5+ years managing and mentoring teams.
Demonstrated ability to solve complex problems, use sound judgment to assess risk, and communicate a clear, compelling, data-informed narrative to stakeholders, in writing and in person.
Strategic thinker with entrepreneurial drive, passion, and the ability to quickly assess product goals and objectives.
Proven ability to build constructive, collaborative relationships with cross-functional stakeholders and across all levels of the company, while modeling Fenix24's Culture and Values.
Excellent analytical and organizational skills.
Proven track record building or leading products in resilience, backup/DR, security operations, exposure management, or asset management.
What Success Looks Like in Year One
A product strategy and Argos99 roadmap that leadership has agreed on and the whole company can explain.
Pricing and packaging validated with MSP/MSSP and enterprise customers.
A product operating rhythm and metrics framework in place, with the first product hires planned.
Salary: $250,000 - $350,000

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.text:
About First Bus:
Are you ready to advance your career with one of the UK's leading bus operators? Join a forward-thinking company that embraces cutting-edge bus technology, from innovative mobile apps to environmentally friendly vehicles. We are passionate about delivering passenger journeys that are sustainable, comfortable, and efficient. We are at the forefront of innovation in the industry, connecting communities and shaping the future of public transport.
Position: Head of Engineering
Location: Home based with travel to our UK based portfolio of Coaching entities.
The Head of Engineering will provide senior engineering leadership across all coach operations, ensuring the consistent application of engineering standards, regulatory compliance and best practice. The role will work closely with the Managing Director Coach, Coaching Directors, General Managers, Operations teams and depot engineering leaders to drive performance, reliability and continuous improvement while supporting the business's commercial, operational and sustainability objectives.
Key Details:
Salary up to £95,000 - £100,000 DOE
Monday-Friday
The Head of Engineering is accountable for establishing and maintaining a robust engineering framework across all coach operations.
Operating as a key member of the Coach Leadership Team, the role holder will provide visible leadership across multiple businesses and locations, ensuring engineering activities support the delivery of safe, reliable and customer-focused transport services.
The role will develop and embed engineering standards, governance and continuous improvement practices while acting as the senior escalation point for complex technical, compliance and fleet performance issues.
Through strong stakeholder engagement and coaching of local engineering leaders, the Head of Engineering will build engineering capability, drive operational performance and support the successful delivery of the Coach strategy.
What We're Looking For:
Significant senior engineering leadership experience within a transport, fleet, automotive, commercial vehicle, coach, bus, logistics or related engineering environment.
Extensive knowledge of vehicle engineering, maintenance management and regulatory compliance requirements.
Proven ability to lead engineering performance improvement across multiple sites or business units.
Strong understanding of engineering governance, risk management and assurance processes.
Demonstrable success in coaching and developing engineering leaders.
Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Strong commercial and financial acumen.
Experience leading transformation, change and continuous improvement initiatives.
Ability to analyse complex operational and technical data to drive performance improvements.
A strategic thinker who is equally comfortable operating at both operational and executive levels.
Professional engineering qualification or equivalent technical experience preferred.
Applicants are advised that background checks will be conducted as a standard part of our recruitment process and to comply with UK employment requirements, we ask all applicants to confirm their right to work in the UK.
Rewards:
• Your health is important to us which is why we offer Simply Health & Smart Health for you and your dependents at no cost to you! This offering includes cash-back benefits across optical & dental as well as virtual GP appointments, mental health support and nutrition and fitness advise. Our EAP provision offers 24hr, 365 days a year mental health support
• We are also committed to your financial wellbeing, and we offer a platform with many discounts on high street brands and supermarkets etc
• Working at First you also receive discounted train travel for you and your family after 6 months service as well as a free bus pass
• Free onsite parking + cycle to work scheme
• Up to 5 weeks holiday + bank holidays
• Pension scheme and chance to buy discounted FirstGroup shares

jobs.title: Director, Data Engineering
jobs.text:
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Director of Data Engineering to lead our enterprise data engineering strategy, platform modernization, and operational excellence initiatives. This role will drive the design, governance, reliability, and scalability of our data ecosystem while enabling analytics, AI, and business intelligence capabilities across the organization. The Director will partner with technology and business leaders to deliver secure, trusted, and business-ready data solutions that support organizational growth and innovation.
Define and execute the enterprise data engineering strategy, roadmap, and operating model.
Lead and develop high-performing teams of managers, architects, and data engineers.
Oversee the design, implementation, and optimization of enterprise data platforms, including data warehouses, lakes, lakehouses, and analytical data products.
Establish standards for data architecture, integration, governance, quality, security, observability, and DataOps.
Drive modernization initiatives that improve scalability, reduce technical debt, and enhance operational efficiency.
Enable AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, and self-service reporting through trusted data foundations.
Partner with executive leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to align data initiatives with business objectives.
Manage technology investments, vendor relationships, budgets, and resource planning.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, or related field, or equivalent experience.
12+ years of progressive experience in data engineering, architecture, analytics engineering, or enterprise data platform leadership.
7+ years leading technical teams in complex enterprise environments.
Experience developing enterprise data strategies, governance programs, and modernization roadmaps.
Strong expertise with cloud data platforms, ETL/ELT frameworks, data warehousing, data integration, and production operations.
Advanced SQL skills and experience with relational and analytical databases.
Experience with AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or hybrid cloud environments.
Experience with Informatica or similar enterprise integration platforms.
Preferred Qualifications
Master's degree in a related discipline.
Experience with Informatica IDMC, Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, Airflow, dbt, Azure Data Factory, AWS Glue, Power BI, and related technologies.
Experience supporting AI, machine learning, or advanced analytics initiatives.
Experience leading large-scale data modernization programs in regulated or data-driven industries.
Technical Skills
Enterprise data integration and data management platforms
Cloud-based data architecture and engineering
Data warehousing, lakehouse, and analytical platforms
DataOps, observability, and operational excellence
Data governance, metadata management, and lineage
Modern orchestration and transformation frameworks
Business intelligence and analytics technologies, including Power BI
Agile methodologies, CI/CD pipelines, and source control platforms such as GitHub and GitLab
Project collaboration tools including Jira and Confluence
What We Offer
Competitive salary and performance bonus program
Fully remote work environment
Comprehensive benefits package including 401k match
19 days of PTO per year; 10 holidays per year
Opportunity to work in a mission-driven organization where your work directly shapes clarity, confidence, and better outcomes across healthcare
Travel
Up to 10% travel, based on business needs. While our roles are 100% remote, we do get together a few times a year for up to one week. Employees are given ample notice and attendance is expected.
Work Environment
This position operates primarily in a remote work environment and requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while performing work at a desk or workstation. The employee must be able to operate standard office equipment, including a computer, keyboard, mouse, webcam, and telephone.
The role also requires the ability to occasionally move throughout a workspace to access files, office equipment, and work-related materials. Effective communication, both written and verbal, is essential for interacting with employees, clients, and stakeholders.
Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action Statement
Staritas is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or veteran status.
As a federal contractor, Staritas complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding nondiscrimination and affirmative action. We are committed to creating a workplace that is fair, inclusive, and grounded in merit-based decision-making.
Accommodation Statement
If you need reasonable accommodation to apply for this position, please contact the recruiter.
Pay Transparency Statement
Staritas posts compensation ranges and benefits for all open roles. The base compensation range for this position is $165,000 - $175,000annually, plus a comprehensive benefits package. Compensation offered will depend on factors including experience, skills, geographic location, and internal equity. Staritas does not retaliate against employees or applicants for discussing compensation.
Benefits Statement
Staritas offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial security of our employees. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement savings plans with company contributions; paid time off and company holidays; paid parental and family leave; and access to employee assistance and wellness resources. Additional benefits include life and disability insurance, professional development opportunities, and flexible work arrangements.
Learn more about us by visiting .

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Management
jobs.text:
Position Summary...
What you'll do...
Role summary:
The Senior Director, Product Management, leads the strategic direction and operations for multiple complex product families within Walmart - with a focus on Governance and Corporate Affairs. This role defines long-term product vision, aligns cross-functional teams, and drives innovation by leveraging data and emerging technologies. The position is accountable for enterprise-wide resource allocation, financial planning, and organizational capability development. It requires influencing senior leadership, managing product roadmaps, and ensuring compliance with governance standards. The role fosters a high-performing culture focused on operational excellence, ethical practices, and continuous improvement to deliver impactful business outcomes and maintain Walmart’s competitive positioning.
About the team:
The Corporate Functions Product team develops and scales innovative products, platforms, and AI-enabled solutions to enhance Walmart’s corporate operations. Collaborating with Finance, Corporate Affairs, Legal and Governance, and People teams, the group streamlines workflows, modernizes processes, and improves access to reliable data and insights. The team focuses on reusable capabilities that address enterprise-wide challenges while delivering measurable business outcomes. Members apply strong stakeholder management, program development, and technical expertise to drive impactful solutions supporting strategic goals and operational excellence across the organization.
What you'll do:
Define and lead long-term product strategy and vision for multiple complex product families aligned with business objectives and market trends.
Collaborate with senior leadership to develop and deliver financial plans, resource allocation, and investment recommendations.
Oversee product roadmap prioritization, risk management, and execution to drive growth and innovation.
Foster cross-functional alignment by partnering with Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Business teams to ensure strategic priorities are met.
Guide organizational capability development through talent recruitment, mentorship, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Leverage data analytics and emerging technologies to inform product decisions and enhance competitive positioning.
What you'll bring:
Extensive experience leading product strategy and operations for complex product portfolios.
Proven ability to define long-term vision and align product roadmaps with business objectives.
Strong expertise in cross-functional leadership, collaborating with Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Business teams.
Demonstrated success in data-driven decision making and leveraging AI and emerging technologies.
Skilled in managing resource allocation, risk, and dependencies to deliver financial targets.
Ability to influence senior leadership with fact-based narratives and market insights.
Commitment to developing high-performing teams and fostering continuous learning and innovation.
At Walmart, we offer competitive pay as well as performance-based bonus awards and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet. Health benefits include medical, vision and dental coverage. Financial benefits include 401(k), stock purchase and company-paid life insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO (including sick leave), parental leave, family care leave, bereavement, jury duty, and voting. Other benefits include short-term and long-term disability, company discounts, Military Leave Pay, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, and more. You will also receive PTO and/or PPTO that can be used for vacation, sick leave, holidays, or other purposes. The amount you receive depends on your job classification and length of employment. It will meet or exceed the requirements of paid sick leave laws, where applicable. For information about PTO, see . Live Better U is a Walmart-paid education benefit program for full-time and part-time associates in Walmart and Sam's Club facilities. Programs range from high school completion to bachelor's degrees, including English Language Learning and short-form certificates. Tuition, books, and fees are completely paid for by Walmart.
Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to a specific plan or program terms.
For information about benefits and eligibility, see One.Walmart.
The annual salary range for this position is $160,000.00 - $320,000.00 Additional compensation includes annual or quarterly performance bonuses. Additional compensation for certain positions may also include :
- Stock

jobs.title: Vice President, Product Management
jobs.text:
Magna Legal Services is a trusted nationwide partner to law firms, corporations, insurance carriers, and government agencies, delivering comprehensive legal support at every stage of a case. From court reporting and record retrieval to jury consulting, investigations, litigation graphics, and language services, we help our clients navigate complex legal challenges with confidence. Our reputation is built on the expertise, dedication, and professionalism of our team, and we’re proud to foster a culture where talented people can do meaningful work and grow their careers.
Magna Legal Services is seeking a Vice President of Product Management to build and lead consistent product management practices across the company. Reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, this leader will lead Magna’s product management team and work with Business Unit leadership in a matrixed environment to bring structure, process, and discipline to how Magna evaluates, develops, launches, and improves its products and services.
The VP will contribute to product strategy by bringing client, market, and operational insights to planning and prioritization. Working closely with leaders across Commercial (including Sales, Marketing, and Client Success), Technology, Operations, and Magna’s Business Units, including court reporting, records retrieval, jury consulting, investigations, trial technology, and language services, the VP will help turn strategic priorities into well-defined roadmaps and coordinated execution. Product sits at the center of these groups: the VP serves as the bridge between the Business Units, Technology, Sales, Marketing, and Client Success, and owns enterprise-wide products that do not fall neatly within a single Business Unit, such as the client portal.
Magna’s product managers will report directly to the VP of Product Management, with a dotted line to their respective Business Unit leaders. The dotted-line relationship reflects that the Business Units own their product and offering strategy; product managers will work closely with their Business Unit leaders to ensure product development is directed by and consistent with Business Unit priorities.
The VP will also work through Magna’s Product Council, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, which brings together executive, commercial, and technology leadership, including the CTO, to align product priorities across the company. The VP will partner closely with the CTO and Engineering leadership, who will be actively involved in shaping product priorities, roadmaps, and feasibility decisions, so that product direction and technology strategy move forward together.
Primary Responsibilities
Lead, develop, and manage Magna’s product managers, who report directly to the VP with a dotted line to their Business Unit leaders.
Own the strategy, roadmap, and performance of enterprise-wide products that serve multiple Business Units, such as the client portal.
Establish product management processes, standards, and governance that support consistent decision-making across Magna.
Introduce best practices for product discovery, opportunity assessment, prioritization, requirements development, launch planning, and ongoing improvement.
Contribute to product strategy by sharing client feedback, market insights, portfolio assessments, and product performance data.
Translate company and service-line priorities into clear product roadmaps, business requirements, and execution plans.
Facilitate cross-functional planning and decision-making among Business Unit, Technology, Sales, Marketing, Client Success, and Operations leaders, including through Magna’s Product Council.
Guide product initiatives from initial concept through development, launch, adoption, and refinement.
Develop practical tools and frameworks to evaluate opportunities, build business cases, assess feasibility, and measure expected impact.
Partner with CTO/Engineering team to ensure engineering produces development timelines with enough specificity around milestones and sequencing to enable the PM to monitor and report out on progress.
Define and monitor measures of product performance, such as adoption, client outcomes, revenue contribution, and operational effectiveness.
Identify opportunities to improve existing products and services, and coordinate the work needed to advance them.
Build organizational understanding of product management roles, processes, and decision rights.
Desired Background
Bachelor’s degree in business, technology, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Significant experience in product management, product operations, or product development, ideally in professional services, legal services, technology-enabled services, or a related environment.
Demonstrated success establishing or improving product management processes and cross-functional ways of working.
Experience coordinating products or services through discovery, development, launch, and ongoing improvement.
Strong ability to translate client and business needs into requirements, roadmaps, and actionable plans.
Experience with prioritization, business cases, product performance measures, or go-to-market planning.
Excellent communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to build alignment among senior stakeholders.
Strong organizational and analytical skills, with the judgment to introduce process that supports effective execution.
Comfortable working in a dynamic organization and building structure where processes are still developing.
Success in This Role
Success will mean that Magna has clear, repeatable product management practices; teams have a shared process for assessing and advancing product opportunities; and product decisions are supported by client insight, business priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Magna Legal Services provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.
This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.
