jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
About BusRight
Districts run their bus operations on BusRight every school day. We’ve found product-market fit, and the business is growing. What we build next determines whether we stay a useful tool or become the platform K-12 transportation runs on. Our next Head of Product owns that outcome.
You’ll report to the CPO and own product and design end to end: strategy, roadmap, team and execution. You’ll be hands-on, setting direction, making calls and shipping, while you build the team around you.
What Success Looks Like
You know BusRight’s users, market and product deeply.
The product strategy is sharper and clearer, built on what exists and backed by evidence.
You’ve shipped bets you owned from framing through delivery, and they moved customer and business outcomes.
Product drives BusRight. The right team is in place, and every function builds from its direction.
Customer value is measured and reported across BusRight’s products and services, and that evidence drives roadmap and commercial decisions.
The CPO, CEO and Engineering treat you as a trusted thought partner on where the product goes next.
What You Will Do
Work with the founders to define and pressure-test where BusRight wins.
Translate strategy into a living roadmap where every priority and commitment is tied to the value it delivers.
Own the product lifecycle from discovery through launch and outcome measurement.
Own product analytics, defining how BusRight measures adoption and usage and partnering with CS and Commercial to put those measures to work.
Report on the value customers get from BusRight’s products and services, and use it to guide roadmap and commercial decisions.
Make the hard calls on what not to build, and what to give up on when it isn’t working.
Partner with Engineering to ship reliably at scale without losing speed.
Stay in direct contact with users and customers. This role doesn't delegate learning.
Represent product in board conversations, partner discussions, and recruiting
Hire, develop and retain a world-class product and design team as we scale.
Hold the product team to a high bar of rigor, craft and accountability to outcomes, not output.
Build a product-led culture across BusRight, where every team understands customer value and brings evidence to its decisions.
What We Are Looking For
Leadership experience: 3–5 years in product leadership, with meaningful time at early-stage or high-growth companies.
Product-market fit: found it rather than inherited it. In the room while the answer was still unclear, made bets, got some wrong, cracked it, and can tell that story in detail.
Consumer product experience: a feel for what makes people love a product and come back to it. EdTech is a plus, not a requirement.
Product and design ownership: has led product design as well as product management.
Team building: a track record of hiring and developing strong PMs at early-stage companies.
Metrics-oriented: frames problems in numbers, sets clear success measures and knows when the data is strong enough to act on.
Technical depth: works through trade-offs with engineers. Coding is a plus, not a requirement.
AI-native: uses AI to research, analyze, prototype and validate, knows where it belongs in the product, and sets the standard for how the team uses it.
Ownership mindset: sees what needs doing and does it without being asked.

jobs.title: Director, Machine Learning Engineering
jobs.text:
About the role
Chime's Data Science & Machine Learning team powers decisions across the company, from how we protect members to how we build products for them. We're looking for a Director to lead that team through its biggest shift yet: moving from traditional models to a modern, AI-driven approach built on transformers and foundation models. You'll lead managers and staff-level engineers, define what great ML looks like at Chime's scale, and rebuild the practice around it. If you want to shape the future of ML at a company where it directly affects members' financial lives, this is the role.
In this role, you can expect to
Lead and grow Chime's ML organization, managing managers and staff-level engineers across all of Chime's ML work.
Set the vision and roadmap for moving Chime's models from traditional approaches to transformer- and foundation-model-based systems.
Coach your managers to build strong, high-performing teams, and raise the technical bar across the practice.
Shape the architecture of Chime's ML platform, including how we train, fine-tune, serve and scale models on a modern GPU-based stack.
Define what good ML looks like at Chime: standards for model development, evaluation, deployment and monitoring.
Partner with product, engineering, risk and business leaders to turn ML into measurable impact for members.
Make the call on when to build, buy or fine-tune, and explain the trade-offs clearly to executives.
To thrive in this role, you have
Deep machine learning expertise, with a well-formed point of view on transformer and foundation models and where they do (and don't) beat traditional approaches.
Familiarity with GPUs and the modern ML stack, from training and fine-tuning to serving models in production at scale.
Experience managing managers and staff-level ICs, with the technical credibility to earn their trust.
A track record of building or transforming an ML practice: hiring, setting standards and growing leaders.
Experience setting a multi-year ML strategy and turning it into shipped results.
Clear communication with executives and cross-functional partners; you can make complex ML trade-offs easy to follow.
Bonus: experience applying ML in fintech or another regulated industry.

The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.
Wage Notice
$269,000—$373,000 USD
A little about us
At Chime, we believe that everyone can achieve financial progress. We created Chime—a financial technology company, not a bank*—on the premise that core banking services should be helpful, easy, and free. Through our user-friendly tools and intuitive platforms, we empower our members to take control of their finances and work towards their goals. Whether it's starting a savings account, purchasing a first car or home, launching a business, or pursuing higher education, we're proud to have helped millions unlock their financial potential.
We're a team of problem solvers, dreamers, and builders with one shared obsession: our members. From day one, Chimers have worked tirelessly to out-hustle and out-execute competitors to bring our mission to life. Their grit and determination inspire us to work harder every day to deliver the very best experience possible. We each bring an owner's mindset to our work, refusing to be outdone and holding ourselves accountable to meet and exceed the highest bars for our teams, our company, and our members.
We believe in being bold, dreaming big, and taking risks, while also working together, embracing our diverse perspectives, and giving each other honest feedback. Our culture remains deeply entrepreneurial, encouraging every Chimer to see themselves as stewards of our mission to help everyday Americans unlock their financial progress.
We know that to achieve our mission, we must earn and keep people's trust—so we hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity in everything we do. These aren't just words on a wall—our values are embedded in every aspect of our business, serving as a north star that guides us as we work to help millions achieve their financial potential.
Because if we don't—who will?
*Chime is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. or Stride Bank, N.A., Members FDIC.
What we offer for our full-time, regular employees
🏢 Our in-office work policy is designed to keep you connected - with four days a week in the office and Fridays from home for those near one of our offices, plus team and company-wide events depending on location.
💻 Benefits that support your work and life, including backup child, elder, and pet care and subsidized commuter benefits for eligible employees.
✨ Comprehensive health, financial, and wellbeing benefits designed to support you at every stage of life.
🏝 Generous vacation policy and company-wide paid days off
🫂 1% of your time off to support local community organizations of your choice
👟 Annual wellness stipend to use towards eligible wellness related expenses
👶 Up to 22 weeks of paid parental leave for birthing parents and 12 weeks of paid parental leave for non-birthing parents
👪 Access to family planning reimbursement
💚 A challenging and fulfilling opportunity to join one of the most experienced teams in FinTech and help millions unlock financial progress
We know that great work can’t be done without a diverse team and inclusive environment. That’s why we specifically look for individuals of varying strengths, skills, backgrounds, and ideas to join our team. We believe this gives us a competitive advantage to better serve our members and helps us all grow as Chimers and individuals.
Chime is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Cook County Ordinance, NYC Fair Chance Act, and the LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and consistent with Canadian provincial and federal laws. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during any stage of the application process, please contact: accommodations@chime.com.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.text:
Role Summary
Responsibilities: Lead an established, talented Engineering team with strong, documented ways of working as we launch our first SaaS product, a competitive platform built on our deep industry expertise and direct relationships with clients. This is a highly visible role, working closely with business leaders to shape our technical strategy, including how we build AI into new and existing products.
Salary: £90,00 to £110,000 per annum depending on prior experience
Benefits: Discretionary profit share bonuses paid twice per year, hybrid and flexible working options, generous holiday allowance, private medical insurance, critical illness cover, income protection, full funding for external training and more
Role Type: Full or part-time, permanent position. Our standard working week is 37.5 hours, Monday to Friday, however we can also consider applicants looking for part-time hours of 30 hours per week
Start Date: The role will ideally commence in January 2027, but we also have start dates available every month of the year. You will be asked to state your availability on your application form
Application Deadlines: Whilst there are no set application deadlines, we strongly recommend applying as early as possible. The role will close when a suitable candidate is found
Location: This role is available in our Global Headquarters in Cambridge or our London offices. Company-funded travel between the two offices will be required, as the Engineering team is based across both locations
About the Role
Costello Medical is entering an exciting new chapter. As a highly innovation-focused business, we have invested heavily in building our first SaaS product entirely in-house, and it is now ready for launch. We are looking for an experienced engineering leader to guide our development team through launch, early go-to-market and post-launch phases. The successful candidate will continue to develop a competitive product that grows its market share by drawing on the direct client relationships established through our services work. You will join at the point of product launch, so you will have real ownership of making the launch a success, the post-launch roadmap and guiding the product lifecycle and strategy.
You will join a talented, established in-house development team of eight, including software engineers, a Front-End Lead and a Back-End & AI Lead, and work alongside our dedicated Innovation team. You will set the overall strategy, best practices and standards for how the team works, giving you a rare opportunity to shape both a product and an engineering culture at a pivotal moment for the company.
This is a senior, highly visible role with real influence across the business. You will act as a trusted technical adviser to company leaders, consulting on the right technical solutions to business challenges, and partner with product owners to turn their ideas into robust, buildable software architecture, then oversee its delivery within the Engineering team. You will also play a key part in our AI strategy, ensuring AI capabilities are built into new and existing products and contributing to our AI leadership team as a strategic adviser, while integrating Engineering closely with collaborating teams to bring new and existing products to success.
Alongside this, you will have ultimate responsibility for the smooth running of the Engineering function, including platform stability and uptime, security by design and compliance, and incident response management, as well as managing our technology supplier portfolio. We are looking for someone with proven strength in software architecture, team strategy and leadership, process management and team building.
Key responsibilities for the role include:
Leading the Engineering team, with overall accountability for its growth, wellbeing and performance, supporting and developing the Engineering management team, and mentoring future leaders within the team
Setting team structure, objectives and hiring plans, and leading a positive team culture where everyone thrives
Defining and embedding the team’s ways of working, including development standards, code review, release management and quality assurance
Owning the engineering roadmap for our first SaaS product, from launch readiness through to developing, growing, scaling and maturing the product
Reviewing and signing off solution designs with product owners, making sure they are scalable, secure and deliverable within the team’s capacity
Working with company leaders to align Engineering strategies with wider company priorities, scope technical solutions and prioritise projects and resources, including deciding whether to build, buy or enable teams to deliver solutions
Shaping our AI roadmap with the AI leadership team and leading the delivery of AI features across new and existing products
Reviewing and maintaining our monitoring, service levels and incident response processes that keep our platforms stable and available
Embedding security by design and maintaining compliance with relevant standards and client requirements, in collaboration with our inhouse IT and Legal teams
Building feedback loops with client-facing teams so that customer insight shapes the product roadmap
Building a strong internal network and team culture that raises the visibility of the Engineering team and its capabilities across the company, and keeps the team close to what client-facing teams need
Selecting, contracting and managing the Engineering team’s technology suppliers, balancing cost, risk and performance
Career Profile
To learn more about the personal and professional development opportunities at Costello Medical, explore first-hand career profiles from our colleagues about their experiences with the company: https://www.costellomedical.co.uk/careers/working-at-costello-medical/
About Costello Medical
Costello Medical is a rapidly growing global healthcare agency specialising in medical communications, market access and health economic and outcomes research. We work with a wide range of clients, including the industry’s most successful pharmaceutical and medical technology companies, patient and public health bodies and charitable organisations.
Technology and innovation sit at the heart of how we work. We are always looking for best-of-breed software and have built a strong internal technology stack, but we are equally willing to build our own solutions where they bring genuine value and opportunities that off-the-shelf products cannot. Our Engineering team sits at the forefront of digital innovation for our scientific teams, turning their expertise into digital tools and products.
We have been listed in the Top 100 Best Companies to Work For list since 2017, the Boston Globe’s Top Places to Work list in 2025 and were proud to receive B Corporation accreditation in 2022. Learn more about us, our work, and our mission on our website: https://www.costellomedical.com/

jobs.title: Regional Head of Product Proposition (General Insurance)
jobs.text:
ABOUT US:
PolicyStreet is a leading InsurTech group backed by Khazanah, specialising in innovative digital insurance solutions for businesses and consumers in Southeast Asia and Australia. With a network of over 40 providers, we offer a comprehensive range of products, including embedded insurance, customised employee benefits, car insurance renewals, financial advisory, and digital solutions – making insurance straightforward, for everyone. Through our regional group of companies, we serve more than 5 million customers with over US$ 4 billion in sum insured.
THE WORKING CULTURE:
You’ll work closely with our Founders and C-suite, ensuring that decisions are made quickly, feedback is direct, and good work is visible.
We move faster than a traditional insurer, while respecting regulatory requirements and portfolio health.
If you’re solid in the fundamentals, and want the products you develop to actually reach the market – join us in shaping how GI is done in a more digital, partner-led environment.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Develop and execute the regional product strategy and roadmap aligned with the company's business objectives and growth plans.
Structure and own insurance products end-to-end across commercial (All Risk, Cyber) and personal lines (Extended Warranty, Travel, etc.), ensuring coverage relevance, pricing discipline, and scalability for digital distribution.
Partner closely with Partnership Managers to structure and tailor products for digital and embedded solutions, translating partner needs into viable, compliant insurance propositions.
Manage product rates and pricing frameworks, working closely with insurers to balance competitiveness, loss ratios, and underwriting appetite.
Act as the key liaison between insurers and partners, driving alignment on product design, terms, and ongoing enhancements.
Lead and coach regional team in building a culture of accountability, collaboration and strong product thinking.
Build a high-performing team that balances strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
Promote a customer-centric, data-informed and commercially accountable approach to product management.

jobs.title: Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO)
jobs.text:
Workana · Remote, LATAM · Reports to Tomás O'Farrell (CEO)
The Opportunity
We are reinventing Workana, and we’re looking for the person who will lead Product and Technology to build the next version of our platform, with a dedicated Product and Development team to make it happen.
Workana connects companies with top talent across Latin America, from individual specialists to cross-functional teams and outcome-based projects. More than 2 million professionals join Workana every year, and over 500,000 companies have hired through the platform. Every placement helps a company scale faster and opens a new career path for someone talented.
This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll define what we build and why, and you’ll get into the details yourself: prototyping, discussing architecture and code with the team, and using the product every day, so you always know what’s working, what isn’t, and what we should try next.
The objective is simple and ambitious: help companies and talent navigate the biggest shift in work in decades. AI is automating tasks, but most work isn’t disappearing, it’s being redesigned. Great talent is no longer the one who executes a task well, but the one who understands the problem, redesigns the workflow and owns the result. We want Workana to be where companies find that talent, and where talent becomes it.
Where Do You Shine?
This is the most important part of the role.
Truly AI-native
AI has completely changed the way you work: how you research, prototype, decide and build. Your week today looks nothing like it did two years ago, and you can show us exactly why. And you know how to bring that into the product: you design experiences where AI does the work for the user, not just another feature in the menu.
Product judgment
You live and breathe what makes a product great and what doesn't. We take the process (UX, PRDs, discovery) for granted; what we're looking for is taste and genuine curiosity. You can tell us why a product you used this year truly surprised you, and you understand the dynamics of a two-sided marketplace: trust, match quality and recurrence.
Ship, learn, iterate
You turn ideas into working product in days, not months. You launch, measure what happened and iterate fast, and you know that with AI the gap between an idea and production keeps shrinking. Speed never comes at the cost of quality: you build the habits and systems that let the team do both.
Leadership and storytelling
A great vision is worthless if it doesn't spread. You know how to align engineering, business and operations behind the same idea, and get everyone pushing in the same direction.
If these four areas are not where you have personally delivered strong results, this probably isn't the right role for you.
What You'll Build
AI is redesigning work, and our freelancers' work is no exception. To lead that shift, we start from something no one else has: ten years of real work across Latin America, with more than 11 million profiles and around 25K projects posted every month. Today we barely use that data.
Your job is to turn it into Workana Intelligence, an intelligence layer that understands both sides:
For clients: stop buying a catalog of profiles and start buying outcomes. Understand their business problem, design the mix of AI and talent that best solves it, and orchestrate the delivery.
For talent: know who truly delivers, beyond their skills, and give each person the opportunities, validation and training that help them grow.
What You'll Do
Define the product and technology vision and strategy, and turn them into a roadmap built on a few high-impact bets.
Build the machine that turns ideas into production: a team and a way of working that ship fast and with high quality, using AI to shorten every step from idea to deploy.
Be the voice of our users in every decision: what frustrates them, what they love, and what they don’t yet know they need. And make sure that insight shows up in the product in weeks, not quarters.
Decide what gets built, what doesn’t, and to what level of finish. Saying no to a bad idea is easy; the real work is saying no to a good idea that arrived at the wrong time.
Launch, measure and iterate: put things in users’ hands early, learn from what happens and adjust fast.
Build a team that talented people want to join and grow in, and own the platform: architecture, quality, security and costs.

jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.text:
Exthymic is an early-stage deep-tech startup on a mission to prevent millions of cancer deaths by making curative cell therapies widely accessible. Our platform enables patient-specific treatment manufacturing at the point of care, overcoming the limits of centralized biopharma models. Led by experienced industry pioneers, we blend hardware, software, and biological engineering to disrupt the status quo and democratize life-saving therapies. Join us to solve complex challenges and drive global healthcare innovation.
About You:
You have deep experience standing up and operating a product function. You've worked in and across the cell and gene therapy ecosystem, you know how cell therapies are made and where manufacturing breaks down, and you understand how to bring a complex device, drug, or combination product to market. You've navigated regulatory uncertainty, learned new scientific concepts, and developed a product strategy that spans diverse customer types and timelines. You get up to speed on a new product and its users fast, and you establish the development processes that bring it to market.
You visit labs and clinical sites, build relationships, and see how people work today. You translate what you learn into market and customer needs and product requirements, test them with a range of potential customers, and keep them up to date as development progresses.
You are the guiding voice in product direction. You'll work directly with our leadership team and with our engineering and science leads. When we debate direction, you make the case for the customer, backed by data.
This role may start without direct reports. You'll do the work yourself at first and build a team as the product function grows. You'd rather build than inherit a product organization.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Shape the product direction. Recommend where the product should go for the current platform and what comes after it, and back it with data. Push back when the market doesn't support a direction we like. Keep the direction current as science, engineering, the market, and the regulatory landscape change.
Own the product roadmap. Keep the roadmap and the timeline to our major product milestones. Set priorities, and trade off scope, schedule, and customer needs.
Know our customers and the market. Decide which customers we serve first and what they need from us. Spend time with the clinicians, scientists, and health system leaders who would use, buy, and approve a cell processing platform. Learn how they work, what the product has to fit into, and what would get them to adopt it. Know the competitive, technology, and regulatory landscape, and tell us what it means for our product.
Own the product requirements. Write the customer needs, user stories, and product requirements. Test them with users and buyers, and revise them as you learn.
Keep requirements and design aligned. Work with systems engineering, who maintain the requirements and verify the build against them, to keep requirements current as the science and design evolve. Agree with engineering, biology, regulatory, and quality on how customer needs become design inputs, and make sure every requirement traces back to a customer need.
Own the product development process. Run our product development process and keep making it better: how requirements mature, how releases are scoped and reviewed, and how decisions get made and documented.
Build the product function. Start as a hands-on individual contributor. Represent the product to our clinical collaborators and partners. As the function grows, hire and lead a product team.

jobs.text:
Job Title: Director of Engineering, Internal Platforms
Job Type: Full-time
Location: Remote
The Role
We’re looking for a highly technical, hands-on Director of Engineering to lead the architecture, development, and scalability of the internal platforms powering our operations, data workflows, and business ecosystem.
You’ll own the engineering direction of mission-critical systems while overseeing quality engineering, ensuring our platforms are reliable, scalable, and built for automation.
This role requires a strong technical leader who stays close to the code, drives architectural decisions, and leverages AI-powered tools and modern engineering practices to accelerate development. You’ll lead engineering teams, establish technical standards, and deliver systems that simplify complex operations at scale.
What You’ll Be Doing
Lead Internal Platform Engineering: Own the architecture, development, and scalability of platforms supporting operational workflows, expert lifecycle management, data collection, analytics, and business processes.
Build Intelligent Systems: Integrate LLMs, AI agents, and automation into internal platforms to streamline workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve operational efficiency.
Drive Platform Architecture: Design scalable APIs, distributed services, event-driven systems, and integrations connecting onboarding, assessments, subscriptions, data pipelines, and financial workflows.
Own Quality Engineering: Lead QE strategy, automated testing frameworks, CI/CD quality gates, release validation, and production reliability across platforms.
Advance Testing Automation: Implement AI-assisted testing, automated regression coverage, and evaluation frameworks for traditional and AI-powered applications.
Stay Hands-On: Drive technical design, contribute to implementation, review code, troubleshoot production issues, and resolve complex engineering challenges.
Improve Engineering Productivity: Introduce AI-assisted development workflows, developer tooling, and automation to accelerate delivery while maintaining engineering quality.
Lead Engineering Teams: Mentor engineers, establish technical standards, drive execution, and foster a culture of ownership, experimentation, and accountability.
Partner Cross-Functionally: Work with Product, AI/ML, Data, and Operations to translate business needs into scalable technical solutions.
What We’re Looking For
10+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years in engineering leadership roles.
Strong hands-on development expertise in Python, TypeScript, or similar languages, with recent experience building and debugging production systems.
Deep experience in platform architecture, including distributed systems, microservices, APIs, event-driven architectures, and workflow orchestration.
Practical experience with AI-powered systems, including LLM integrations, agentic workflows, RAG, and evaluation frameworks.
Experience leveraging AI development tools and automation to improve engineering productivity and delivery.
Strong Quality Engineering expertise, including automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, API and end-to-end testing, and production reliability.
Cloud infrastructure proficiency with AWS, GCP, or Azure, Kubernetes, databases, observability, and DevOps practices.
Experience building internal platforms supporting operational workflows, data pipelines, analytics, or complex business processes.
Proven technical leadership, with the ability to mentor engineers, make architectural decisions, and deliver in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in AI research labs, AI-native companies, or high-growth technology startups.
Experience with human data platforms, including expert management, data annotation, human-in-the-loop workflows, data curation, and AI evaluation pipelines.
Familiarity with LLM training and evaluation workflows, including human feedback, preference data, and model benchmarking.
Experience with agent orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, Temporal, or similar technologies.
Experience building internal developer platforms, shared infrastructure, or self-service engineering tools.
Familiarity with AI-assisted testing, automated test generation, and evaluation of nondeterministic systems.

The national pay range for this full-time position is base salary of $280,000 –$350,000. All employees are eligible for equity compensation, and employees may also receive performance-based bonuses, dependent on role and subject to company policies. micro1 provides a comprehensive benefits package, including up to 100% reimbursement for health-insurance premiums, paid time off, a 401(K) plan with a company match, and additional benefits designed to support a high-performing, remote-first workforce.

jobs.title: Director, Product Security, PSIRT
jobs.text:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
Within the Product Security team, our Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) owns Okta's response when a security vulnerability in our products is reported, exploited, or puts customers at risk, across Okta, Auth0 and the systems they run on. PSIRT triages reports from researchers, customers, our bug bounty program and our own automated discovery, leads each incident from intake to closure, drives fixes with engineering and leadership, and publishes CVEs and security advisories as Okta's CVE Numbering Authority.
AI is changing how vulnerabilities are found, by us and by attackers, and the volume of high-impact reports is rising quickly. We seek a director to lead PSIRT through that change: run day-to-day incident response, build the team and the agentic workflows that let it scale, and be the steady, credible voice for Okta when a vulnerability matters to our customers.
What You Will Do
Lead Okta's PSIRT program across all business units, defining its strategy, roadmap and operating model
Own the vulnerability-handling lifecycle, from intake and triage through remediation, coordinated disclosure and post-incident review, and keep our procedures and runbooks current
Act as senior incident lead on Critical and high-profile vulnerabilities, including industry-wide issues, and make clear calls under pressure
Partner with Engineering leaders to drive fixes and hotfixes on time, while engineering owns remediation
Run coordinated disclosure with researchers and partners, and own Okta's CVE and security advisory process with Customer Trust and Security Communications
Work closely with Cyber Defense, Identity Defense, Legal and Federal teams on exploitation analysis, customer impact and regulatory obligations
Own the bug bounty program and relationships with the security research community
Scale the team with automation and AI: agentic triage, root-cause and variant analysis, and tooling that holds up under a surge in volume
Set and report key performance indicators (time to acknowledge, time to resolve, SLA attainment, advisory timeliness) to security and executive leadership
Brief executives clearly and in proportion to risk, and lead post-incident reviews that feed lessons back into the Secure Development Lifecycle
Maintain and strengthen a team culture of growth, openness, trust, rigor, humility, and mutual support
Lead the process of recruiting great engineers to meet the growth plan for the team in collaboration with our recruiters
Mentor PSIRT and Product Security engineers in their career progression
Represent Okta with authority in industry forums and with customers, researchers and peer PSIRTs
What You Bring
United States citizenship and eligibility to obtain Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance, with active or prior security clearance a plus
Flexibility to travel as needed and maintain availability for off-hours incident response escalation
Extensive background in product security incident response or vulnerability management, including leadership or managerial roles, and a commitment to cultivating high-performing, inclusive, and collaborative teams
Proven track record managing geographically distributed teams that cover incidents across time zones
Hands-on experience leading high-severity vulnerability incidents, from triage and impact analysis through fix validation and public disclosure
Strong technical depth in web application, identity and cloud vulnerabilities, with the ability to reproduce issues and judge exploitability and customer impact
Working knowledge of coordinated disclosure and vulnerability handling standards (ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111, FIRST PSIRT Services Framework) and of CVE and CVSS
Experience running or working closely with a bug bounty program
Working knowledge of compliance frameworks (SOC2, PCI, FedRAMP, et al.)
Exceptional ability to communicate, influence, and articulate vulnerability risk to engineers, executives and customers, including in high-pressure situations
Experience working with cross-functional teams, possessing exceptional stakeholder management skills
Experience applying automation or AI to security operations is a plus

jobs.title: Director, Measurement & Data Science
jobs.text:
$250K base + 10 to 20% annual bonus
Reports to: President
Jump 450 is launching a measurement service in 2027, and we are hiring the person who builds it. You will build and run Jump's measurement offer: our own media mix model, monthly readouts and incrementality tests that show clients which ads really drive sales and where to move budget next.
This is a builder role. You will work hands on with Jump's President to design the product, launch it with our first clients in March and sell it to new ones. As the service grows, you will grow it into a team.
What You Will Do
Build the Product
Build Jump's measurement model across our clients' digital channels, using open source frameworks such as Google Meridian or Robyn as a starting point
Design the monthly readout: what each channel really drove, written so a CMO or CFO can act on it
Build the quarterly budget plan: where to move money next and what the move is worth
Design and run incrementality tests (geo holdouts, conversion lift, matched markets) that prove cause and effect
Build scenario planning: what happens to sales if budget goes up or down
Set the data requirements for new clients and QA the spend, sales and analytics data that feeds the model
Run It for Clients
Lead each measurement engagement from data onboarding to readout
Present results to senior client stakeholders, including marketing and finance leaders
Partner with Jump's paid social, search and programmatic teams so findings turn into budget moves the same week
Explain attribution, lift and model results in plain words, and be honest about what the data can and can't say
Sell and Grow the Service
Pitch the service alongside the President and Jump's new business team
Build the case studies, sales materials and proof points that help us sell it
Hire, train and mentor analysts as the client list grows

jobs.title: Head of Software Architecture
jobs.text:
ABOUT POWER FACTORS
Power Factors is a software and solutions provider leading the next generation of clean energy with Unity, one of the most extensive and widely deployed renewable energy management suites (REMS) in the market. With over 300 GW of wind, solar, and energy storage assets managed worldwide across more than 600 customers and 18,000 sites, Power Factors manages 25% of the world’s renewable energy data.*
Power Factors’ Unity REMS supports the entire energy value chain, from monitoring and controls to market analytics. The company’s suite of open, data-driven applications empowers renewable energy stakeholders to collaborate, automate critical workflows, and make more informed decisions to maximize asset returns. Energy stakeholders receive end-to-end support, including solutions for SCADA & PPC, centralized monitoring, performance management, commercial asset management, and field service management.
With deep domain expertise, AI-powered insights are delivered at scale so businesses can optimize assets, unlock growth, and make smarter decisions as the world rapidly transitions to clean energy. Power Factors fights climate change with code.
*Outside China and India
ABOUT THE ROLE
Power Factors is scaling in complexity — more products, more platforms, more sophisticated buyers, and rapidly rising expectations for AI-native capability across our renewable energy software suite. In that context, the absence of a single, accountable technical vision creates real risk: divergent architectural patterns across verticals, inconsistent approaches to AI and data platform investment, and technical debt that compounds faster than it can be paid down.
The Head of Software Architecture exists to close that gap. This is a hands-on, deeply technical leadership role responsible for defining and enforcing enterprise architecture standards across Power Factors' Product & Technology organization — spanning Platform, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, and CAM/FSM/Product Ops — while personally architecting and prototyping the hardest problems the organization faces, particularly around AI-based product introductions, IoT data acquisition, and multi-tenant SaaS scalability.
This role combines the strategic scope of an enterprise architect with the credibility of a builder who still writes code, reviews pull requests, and is comfortable being the most technical person in the room.
Purpose of the Role
The Head of Software Architecture acts to define, evangelize, and enforce a coherent technical architecture strategy that allows Power Factors to scale product complexity without sacrificing reliability, security, or development velocity.
• Enterprise-wide architectural coherence: Technical decisions across verticals are grounded in shared architectural principles, not siloed team preferences.
• AI-native product development: New AI-based product capabilities are architected end-to-end — from data pipeline to model integration to user-facing experience — rather than bolted on.

Core Responsibilities

• Act as a technical escalation point for the highest-stakes design decisions across the organization
3. AI-Based Product Architecture & Delivery
• Architect and personally help build end-to-end AI-based product capabilities — from data acquisition and model selection through deployment and monitoring
• Define Power Factors' architectural approach to LLM-based products, including use of Model Context Protocol (MCP), retrieval architectures, and agentic workflows
• Evaluate and select development LLMs and AI platforms appropriate for embedding into commercial products
• Own the technical bridge between REMI and other AI-native initiatives and the broader platform architecture
• Bring machine learning and data science expertise to bear on product decisions — model selection, feature engineering, data pipeline design, and MLOps practices
4. Hands-On Development
• Write production code, prototype new architectural patterns, and directly contribute to the hardest technical problems facing the organization
• Lead by example on code quality, testing discipline, and engineering craftsmanship
• Stay close enough to the codebase to make credible, current architectural judgments rather than relying on secondhand reporting
• Build proof-of-concept implementations to de-risk major architectural bets before full team investment
5. IoT, Edge, and Industrial Systems Architecture
• Architect scalable IoT data acquisition systems capable of ingesting, normalizing, and processing high-volume telemetry from distributed renewable energy assets
• Design architecture for edge devices and Power Plant Controllers (PPC), balancing on-site computation, latency constraints, and cloud connectivity

• Apply renewables and energy industry domain knowledge to inform data model, integration, and control system design decisions

• Advance Power Factors' multi-tenant SaaS architecture to support scale, tenant isolation, and configurability without fragmenting the codebase
• Define architectural standards for mobile app development where products extend to field and operations use cases
• Evaluate build-vs-buy and platform consolidation decisions across the technology stack

• Identify, evaluate, and roll out AI development tools that enable a 3–4x productivity improvement across engineering teams
• Define best practices for AI-assisted coding, testing, and code review, balancing speed with quality and security
• Partner with engineering leadership to measure and report on productivity gains from AI tooling adoption

Reporting Line
• Reports to: Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO)

◦ Vertical engineering leaders (Platform, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, CAM/FSM/Product Ops)
◦ Product Management and Product Marketing on AI-based product introductions
◦ CloudOps and Security on infrastructure and compliance posture

• Architecture in service of the business, not architecture for its own sake
• Hands-on credibility over theoretical authority
• Pragmatic standardization — enough consistency to scale, not so much it stifles teams
• AI-first thinking applied responsibly, with attention to data quality, safety, and reliability

Required Experience
• 15–20 years of progressive experience in software engineering, with significant time spent in architecture and technical leadership roles
• Enterprise Architecture & Complex System Design: demonstrated experience architecting large-scale, high-complexity systems with significant operational stakes
• Technical Team Leadership: proven ability to lead and mentor senior engineers and architects across distributed teams
• Trading/Transactional Systems: experience building high-throughput, high-integrity trading or transactional systems where correctness and performance are non-negotiable
• AI Product Delivery: track record architecting and shipping end-to-end AI-based product introductions, from concept to production launch
• Hands-On Development: an architect who still codes — genuinely enjoys building, not just designing
• IoT Data Acquisition: experience with systems that ingest and process high-volume telemetry from distributed physical assets
• Edge Devices & Power Plant Controllers (PPC): familiarity with edge computing architectures and industrial control systems
• Renewables / Energy Industry Experience: ideally direct experience in renewable energy or broader energy sector software (strongly preferred, not required)
• Machine Learning & Data Science: solid working knowledge sufficient to make informed architectural and platform decisions
• MCP & LLM-Based Products: hands-on experience with Model Context Protocol, development LLMs, and building LLM-based product features
• Cloud Platforms: deep experience with GCP and/or AWS at an architectural level
• AI Development Tooling: experience selecting and rolling out AI dev tools that meaningfully increase engineering team productivity
• SaaS & Multi-Tenant Architecture: advanced experience designing and scaling multi-tenant SaaS applications
• Mobile App Development: working knowledge of mobile architecture and delivery, sufficient to guide teams building mobile experiences
Core Capabilities
• Strong systems thinking with the ability to zoom between enterprise strategy and line-level code
• Executive-level communication — able to translate architectural tradeoffs into business terms for the CPTO and executive team
• Comfortable operating with significant technical authority while remaining collaborative and low-ego
• Genuine enthusiasm for staying current with the fast-moving AI and LLM landscape
Background Fit
• Principal Engineer, Distinguished Engineer, VP of Engineering, or Chief Architect background
• Experience operating in a scaling, multi-product SaaS organization
• Comfortable being both the enterprise architecture authority and an individual contributor when the problem demands it
Success Metrics (KPIs)
• Number of AI-based product capabilities architected and shipped to production per year
• Measured productivity gains (velocity, cycle time) attributable to AI development tooling rollout
• Reduction in cross-vertical architectural inconsistency and duplicated platform investment
• System reliability and performance metrics for enterprise-critical and transactional systems
• Adoption rate of architectural standards and reference designs across engineering teams
• Qualitative 360° feedback from engineering leaders on technical leadership effectiveness
What This Role Is Not
This role is not a purely strategic or advisory position removed from the codebase, and it is not a people-management role focused primarily on process and reporting. The Head of Software Architecture is expected to remain a credible, hands-on technical contributor throughout their tenure.
The role also does not own product roadmap prioritization or commercial strategy — those remain with Product Management and the CPTO — but it directly shapes what is technically possible and how quickly it can be delivered.

Our culture runs deep and shows up in how we work together - committed, conscientious and collaborative. jobs.title: Directeur·trice de l'architecture logicielle | Head of Software Architecture
jobs.text:
À PROPOS DE POWER FACTORS
Power Factors est un fournisseur de logiciels et de solutions qui ouvre la voie à la prochaine génération d’énergie propre grâce à Unity, l’une des suites de gestion d’énergie renouvelable (REMS) les plus complètes et les plus largement déployées sur le marché. Avec plus de 300 GW d’actifs éoliens, solaires et de stockage d’énergie gérés dans le monde entier auprès de plus de 600 clients et 18 000 sites, Power Factors gère 25 % des données mondiales sur les énergies renouvelables.*
La suite Unity REMS de Power Factors soutient l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur énergétique, de la surveillance et du contrôle à l’analyse des marchés. L’ensemble d’applications ouvertes et axées sur les données de l’entreprise permet aux parties prenantes du secteur des énergies renouvelables de collaborer, d’automatiser les flux de travail critiques et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées afin de maximiser les rendements des actifs. Les parties prenantes bénéficient d’un soutien de bout en bout, incluant des solutions pour le SCADA et le PPC, la surveillance centralisée, la gestion de la performance, la gestion commerciale des actifs et la gestion des services sur le terrain.
Grâce à une expertise approfondie du domaine, des perspectives propulsées par l’IA sont livrées à grande échelle, permettant aux entreprises d’optimiser leurs actifs, de stimuler leur croissance et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées dans un contexte de transition rapide vers l’énergie propre. Power Factors lutte contre les changements climatiques grâce au code.
*Hors Chine et Inde
À PROPOS DU POSTE
Power Factors prend de l’ampleur en termes de complexité : davantage de produits, de plateformes, d’acheteurs sophistiqués, et des attentes croissantes quant aux capacités natives en IA dans notre suite de logiciels pour les énergies renouvelables. Dans ce contexte, l’absence d’une vision technique unique et imputable crée un risque réel : des schémas architecturaux divergents selon les secteurs verticaux, des approches incohérentes en matière d’investissement dans les plateformes d’IA et de données, et une dette technique qui s’accumule plus vite qu’elle ne peut être résorbée.
Le rôle de directeur·trice de l’architecture logicielle existe pour combler cet écart. Il s’agit d’un poste de leadership technique pratique et hautement spécialisé, chargé de définir et d’appliquer les normes d’architecture d’entreprise à l’échelle de l’organisation Produits et Technologie de Power Factors (couvrant les secteurs Plateforme, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps et CAM/FSM/Ops produit), tout en concevant et en prototypant personnellement les problèmes les plus complexes auxquels l’organisation est confrontée, notamment en matière d’introduction de produits basés sur l’IA, d’acquisition de données IoT et d’évolutivité SaaS multitenant.
Ce poste combine la portée stratégique d’un·e architecte d’entreprise et la crédibilité d’un·e bâtisseur·euse qui continue d’écrire du code, de réviser des demandes de tirage (pull requests) et d’être à l’aise en tant que personne la plus technique dans la salle.
Relevant directement du ou de la Chef·fe des produits et de la technologie (CPTO), la personne titulaire agit comme tissu connectif entre la stratégie organisationnelle du ou de la CPTO et les décisions techniques quotidiennes prises par les équipes d’ingénierie verticales, en collaborant étroitement avec les responsables des secteurs (Plateforme, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, CAM/FSM/Ops produit), la gestion de produit et les équipes CloudOps et Sécurité.
Il est important de noter que ce rôle n’est pas un poste purement stratégique ou consultatif éloigné du code, ni un rôle de gestion axé sur les processus et les rapports. La personne titulaire est appelée à demeurer un·e contributeur·trice technique crédible et actif·ve tout au long de son mandat. Ce poste ne comprend pas non plus la responsabilité de la priorisation de la feuille de route produit ou de la stratégie commerciale, car ces responsabilités demeurent avec la gestion de produit et le ou la CPTO. Il façonne toutefois directement ce qui est techniquement possible et à quelle vitesse cela peut être livré.
CE QUE VOUS FEREZ
Architecture d’entreprise et conception de systèmes complexes
Définir et maintenir les normes d’architecture d’entreprise, les architectures de référence et les garde-fous techniques de Power Factors pour l’ensemble des secteurs verticaux
Diriger les revues architecturales pour les initiatives majeures, en assurant la cohérence, l’évolutivité et la maintenabilité à long terme
Être responsable de la feuille de route technique pour les capacités de plateforme transversales (plateforme de données, couche d’intégration, identité, observabilité)
Concevoir des systèmes complexes à haute disponibilité où l’exactitude, la latence et l’intégrité des données ont des conséquences opérationnelles et commerciales réelles
Collaborer avec les responsables des secteurs verticaux (SCADA, EMS, APM, Plateforme, CloudOps) pour s’assurer que les décisions architecturales locales s’alignent sur la direction d’entreprise
Leadership technique des équipes
Bâtir et diriger une fonction d’architecture distribuée opérant comme une autorité technique de confiance en Grèce, à Montréal et dans d’autres régions
Encadrer les ingénieur·e·s senior·e·s et les responsables en ingénierie en matière de jugement architectural, de conception de systèmes et d’analyse des compromis techniques
Établir et animer des forums de gouvernance architecturale (revues de conception, processus RFC, comités de pilotage technique)
Agir comme point d’escalade technique pour les décisions de conception les plus critiques de l’organisation
Architecture et livraison de produits basés sur l’IA
Concevoir et contribuer personnellement à la construction de capacités de produits basées sur l’IA de bout en bout, de l’acquisition de données et de la sélection de modèles jusqu’au déploiement et à la surveillance
Définir l’approche architecturale de Power Factors pour les produits basés sur les LLM, incluant l’utilisation du Model Context Protocol (MCP), les architectures de récupération et les flux de travail agentiques
Évaluer et sélectionner les LLM de développement et les plateformes d’IA adaptés à l’intégration dans des produits commerciaux
Assurer le pont technique entre REMI et les autres initiatives natives en IA et l’architecture de plateforme globale
Mettre à profit l’expertise en apprentissage automatique et en science des données pour orienter les décisions produit : sélection de modèles, ingénierie des caractéristiques, conception de pipelines de données et pratiques MLOps
Développement pratique
Écrire du code de production, prototyper de nouveaux schémas architecturaux et contribuer directement aux problèmes techniques les plus complexes de l’organisation
Montrer l’exemple en matière de qualité du code, de discipline de test et d’excellence en ingénierie
Rester suffisamment proche du code pour formuler des jugements architecturaux crédibles et actuels, plutôt que de se fier à des rapports de seconde main
Réaliser des implémentations de validation de concept pour réduire les risques liés aux grands paris architecturaux avant l’engagement complet des équipes
Architecture IoT, périphérie et systèmes industriels
Concevoir des systèmes d’acquisition de données IoT évolutifs capables d’ingérer, de normaliser et de traiter des volumes élevés de télémétrie provenant d’actifs d’énergie renouvelable distribués
Définir l’architecture pour les dispositifs de périphérie et les contrôleurs de centrale (PPC), en équilibrant le calcul sur site, les contraintes de latence et la connectivité infonuagique
S’assurer que les approches architecturales tiennent compte de la conformité aux codes du réseau, des exigences de contrôle en temps réel et des réalités opérationnelles des environnements SCADA et EMS
Appliquer la connaissance du domaine des énergies renouvelables et de l’énergie pour orienter les décisions de modélisation des données, d’intégration et de conception des systèmes de contrôle
Architecture infonuagique, SaaS et multitenant
Être responsable de la stratégie d’architecture infonuagique sur GCP et/ou AWS, incluant les postures de coût, de résilience et de sécurité
Faire progresser l’architecture SaaS multitenant de Power Factors pour prendre en charge l’échelle, l’isolation des locataires et la configurabilité sans fragmenter le code
Définir les normes architecturales pour le développement d’applications mobiles là où les produits s’étendent aux cas d’utilisation sur le terrain et en opérations
Évaluer les décisions de construction ou d’achat et de consolidation de plateformes à travers la pile technologique
Productivité de l’ingénierie et développement assisté par l’IA
Identifier, évaluer et déployer des outils de développement IA qui permettent une amélioration de la productivité de 3 à 4 fois au sein des équipes d’ingénierie
Définir les meilleures pratiques pour la programmation, les tests et la revue de code assistés par l’IA, en équilibrant vitesse, qualité et sécurité
Collaborer avec la direction de l’ingénierie pour mesurer et communiquer les gains de productivité issus de l’adoption des outils d’IA
Indicateurs de succès
Nombre de capacités de produits basées sur l’IA conçues et mises en production par année
Gains de productivité mesurés (vélocité, délai de cycle) attribuables au déploiement des outils de développement IA
Réduction des incohérences architecturales entre secteurs verticaux et des investissements de plateforme dupliqués
Métriques de fiabilité et de performance des systèmes critiques d’entreprise et transactionnels
Taux d’adoption des normes architecturales et des conceptions de référence à travers les équipes d’ingénierie
Rétroaction qualitative à 360° des responsables en ingénierie sur l’efficacité du leadership technique
CE QUE VOUS DEVEZ APPORTER
15 à 20 ans d’expérience progressive en génie logiciel, avec une part importante consacrée à l’architecture et aux rôles de leadership technique
Expérience démontrée dans la conception de systèmes à grande échelle et haute complexité avec des enjeux opérationnels importants
Capacité avérée à diriger et à encadrer des ingénieur·e·s et des architectes senior·e·s au sein d’équipes distribuées
Expérience dans la conception de systèmes transactionnels ou de trading à haut débit et haute intégrité où l’exactitude et la performance sont non négociables
Bilan avéré dans la conception et la mise en production de produits basés sur l’IA de bout en bout, du concept au lancement en production
Approche pratique du développement : un·e architecte qui code encore et qui prend un réel plaisir à construire, et pas seulement à concevoir

ABOUT THE ROLE
Power Factors is scaling in complexity — more products, more platforms, more sophisticated buyers, and rapidly rising expectations for AI-native capability across our renewable energy software suite. In that context, the absence of a single, accountable technical vision creates real risk: divergent architectural patterns across verticals, inconsistent approaches to AI and data platform investment, and technical debt that compounds faster than it can be paid down.
The Head of Software Architecture exists to close that gap. This is a hands-on, deeply technical leadership role responsible for defining and enforcing enterprise architecture standards across Power Factors' Product & Technology organization — spanning Platform, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, and CAM/FSM/Product Ops — while personally architecting and prototyping the hardest problems the organization faces, particularly around AI-based product introductions, IoT data acquisition, and multi-tenant SaaS scalability.
This role combines the strategic scope of an enterprise architect with the credibility of a builder who still writes code, reviews pull requests, and is comfortable being the most technical person in the room.
Purpose of the Role
The Head of Software Architecture acts to define, evangelize, and enforce a coherent technical architecture strategy that allows Power Factors to scale product complexity without sacrificing reliability, security, or development velocity.
• Enterprise-wide architectural coherence: Technical decisions across verticals are grounded in shared architectural principles, not siloed team preferences.
• AI-native product development: New AI-based product capabilities are architected end-to-end — from data pipeline to model integration to user-facing experience — rather than bolted on.
• Development velocity multiplication: Engineering teams are equipped with modern AI-assisted development tooling and workflows that materially increase throughput.
• Deep technical credibility: Engineering leaders and individual contributors alike see this role as a working architect, not a slide-deck strategist.
• Domain-informed design: Architecture decisions reflect genuine understanding of renewable energy operations — SCADA, EMS, PPC, edge devices, and grid-facing data systems.
This role acts as the connective tissue between the CPTO's organizational strategy and the day-to-day technical decisions made by vertical engineering teams.
Core Responsibilities
1. Enterprise Architecture & Complex System Design
• Define and maintain Power Factors' enterprise architecture standards, reference architectures, and technical guardrails across all verticals
• Lead architectural reviews for major initiatives, ensuring consistency, scalability, and long-term maintainability
• Own the technical roadmap for cross-cutting platform capabilities (data platform, integration layer, identity, observability)
• Design for complex, high-availability systems where correctness, latency, and data integrity carry real operational and commercial consequences
• Partner with vertical leaders (SCADA, EMS, APM, Platform, CloudOps) to ensure local architecture decisions align with enterprise direction
2. Technical Team Leadership
• Build and lead a distributed architecture function that operates as a trusted technical authority across Greece, Montreal, and other regions
• Mentor senior engineers and engineering leaders on architectural judgment, system design, and technical tradeoff analysis
• Establish and run architecture governance forums (design reviews, RFC processes, technical steering committees)
• Act as a technical escalation point for the highest-stakes design decisions across the organization
3. AI-Based Product Architecture & Delivery
• Architect and personally help build end-to-end AI-based product capabilities — from data acquisition and model selection through deployment and monitoring
• Define Power Factors' architectural approach to LLM-based products, including use of Model Context Protocol (MCP), retrieval architectures, and agentic workflows
• Evaluate and select development LLMs and AI platforms appropriate for embedding into commercial products
• Own the technical bridge between REMI and other AI-native initiatives and the broader platform architecture
• Bring machine learning and data science expertise to bear on product decisions — model selection, feature engineering, data pipeline design, and MLOps practices
4. Hands-On Development
• Write production code, prototype new architectural patterns, and directly contribute to the hardest technical problems facing the organization
• Lead by example on code quality, testing discipline, and engineering craftsmanship
• Stay close enough to the codebase to make credible, current architectural judgments rather than relying on secondhand reporting
• Build proof-of-concept implementations to de-risk major architectural bets before full team investment
5. IoT, Edge, and Industrial Systems Architecture
• Architect scalable IoT data acquisition systems capable of ingesting, normalizing, and processing high-volume telemetry from distributed renewable energy assets
• Design architecture for edge devices and Power Plant Controllers (PPC), balancing on-site computation, latency constraints, and cloud connectivity
• Ensure architectural approaches account for grid code compliance, real-time control requirements, and the operational realities of SCADA and EMS environments
• Apply renewables and energy industry domain knowledge to inform data model, integration, and control system design decisions
6. Cloud, SaaS, and Multi-Tenant Architecture
• Own cloud architecture strategy across GCP and/or AWS, including cost, resilience, and security posture
• Advance Power Factors' multi-tenant SaaS architecture to support scale, tenant isolation, and configurability without fragmenting the codebase
• Define architectural standards for mobile app development where products extend to field and operations use cases
• Evaluate build-vs-buy and platform consolidation decisions across the technology stack
7. Engineering Productivity & AI-Enabled Development
• Identify, evaluate, and roll out AI development tools that enable a 3–4x productivity improvement across engineering teams
• Define best practices for AI-assisted coding, testing, and code review, balancing speed with quality and security
• Partner with engineering leadership to measure and report on productivity gains from AI tooling adoption
Reporting & Operating Model
Reporting Line

Embedded collaboration with:
◦ Vertical engineering leaders (Platform, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, CAM/FSM/Product Ops)
◦ Product Management and Product Marketing on AI-based product introductions
◦ CloudOps and Security on infrastructure and compliance posture
Operating Principles
• Architecture in service of the business, not architecture for its own sake
• Hands-on credibility over theoretical authority
• Pragmatic standardization — enough consistency to scale, not so much it stifles teams
• AI-first thinking applied responsibly, with attention to data quality, safety, and reliability
Skills & Profile
Required Experience
• 15–20 years of progressive experience in software engineering, with significant time spent in architecture and technical leadership roles
• Enterprise Architecture & Complex System Design: demonstrated experience architecting large-scale, high-complexity systems with significant operational stakes
• Technical Team Leadership: proven ability to lead and mentor senior engineers and architects across distributed teams
• Trading/Transactional Systems: experience building high-throughput, high-integrity trading or transactional systems where correctness and performance are non-negotiable
• AI Product Delivery: track record architecting and shipping end-to-end AI-based product introductions, from concept to production launch
• Hands-On Development: an architect who still codes — genuinely enjoys building, not just designing
• IoT Data Acquisition: experience with systems that ingest and process high-volume telemetry from distributed physical assets
• Edge Devices & Power Plant Controllers (PPC): familiarity with edge computing architectures and industrial control systems
• Renewables / Energy Industry Experience: ideally direct experience in renewable energy or broader energy sector software (strongly preferred, not required)
• Machine Learning & Data Science: solid working knowledge sufficient to make informed architectural and platform decisions
• MCP & LLM-Based Products: hands-on experience with Model Context Protocol, development LLMs, and building LLM-based product features
• Cloud Platforms: deep experience with GCP and/or AWS at an architectural level
• AI Development Tooling: experience selecting and rolling out AI dev tools that meaningfully increase engineering team productivity
• SaaS & Multi-Tenant Architecture: advanced experience designing and scaling multi-tenant SaaS applications
• Mobile App Development: working knowledge of mobile architecture and delivery, sufficient to guide teams building mobile experiences
Core Capabilities
• Strong systems thinking with the ability to zoom between enterprise strategy and line-level code
• Executive-level communication — able to translate architectural tradeoffs into business terms for the CPTO and executive team
• Comfortable operating with significant technical authority while remaining collaborative and low-ego
• Genuine enthusiasm for staying current with the fast-moving AI and LLM landscape
Background Fit
• Principal Engineer, Distinguished Engineer, VP of Engineering, or Chief Architect background
• Experience operating in a scaling, multi-product SaaS organization
• Comfortable being both the enterprise architecture authority and an individual contributor when the problem demands it
Success Metrics (KPIs)
• Number of AI-based product capabilities architected and shipped to production per year
• Measured productivity gains (velocity, cycle time) attributable to AI development tooling rollout
• Reduction in cross-vertical architectural inconsistency and duplicated platform investment
• System reliability and performance metrics for enterprise-critical and transactional systems
• Adoption rate of architectural standards and reference designs across engineering teams
• Qualitative 360° feedback from engineering leaders on technical leadership effectiveness
What This Role Is Not
This role is not a purely strategic or advisory position removed from the codebase, and it is not a people-management role focused primarily on process and reporting. The Head of Software Architecture is expected to remain a credible, hands-on technical contributor throughout their tenure.
The role also does not own product roadmap prioritization or commercial strategy — those remain with Product Management and the CPTO — but it directly shapes what is technically possible and how quickly it can be delivered.

blocks.text: À PROPOS DE POWER FACTORS

Power Factors est un fournisseur de logiciels et de solutions qui ouvre la voie à la prochaine génération d’énergie propre grâce à Unity, l’une des suites de gestion d’énergie renouvelable (REMS) les plus complètes et les plus largement déployées sur le marché. Avec plus de 300 GW d’actifs éoliens, solaires et de stockage d’énergie gérés dans le monde entier auprès de plus de 600 clients et 18 000 sites, Power Factors gère 25 % des données mondiales sur les énergies renouvelables.*

La suite Unity REMS de Power Factors soutient l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur énergétique, de la surveillance et du contrôle à l’analyse des marchés. L’ensemble d’applications ouvertes et axées sur les données de l’entreprise permet aux parties prenantes du secteur des énergies renouvelables de collaborer, d’automatiser les flux de travail critiques et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées afin de maximiser les rendements des actifs. Les parties prenantes bénéficient d’un soutien de bout en bout, incluant des solutions pour le SCADA et le PPC, la surveillance centralisée, la gestion de la performance, la gestion commerciale des actifs et la gestion des services sur le terrain.

Grâce à une expertise approfondie du domaine, des perspectives propulsées par l’IA sont livrées à grande échelle, permettant aux entreprises d’optimiser leurs actifs, de stimuler leur croissance et de prendre des décisions plus éclairées dans un contexte de transition rapide vers l’énergie propre. Power Factors lutte contre les changements climatiques grâce au code.
*Hors Chine et Inde
À PROPOS DU POSTE

Power Factors prend de l’ampleur en termes de complexité : davantage de produits, de plateformes, d’acheteurs sophistiqués, et des attentes croissantes quant aux capacités natives en IA dans notre suite de logiciels pour les énergies renouvelables. Dans ce contexte, l’absence d’une vision technique unique et imputable crée un risque réel : des schémas architecturaux divergents selon les secteurs verticaux, des approches incohérentes en matière d’investissement dans les plateformes d’IA et de données, et une dette technique qui s’accumule plus vite qu’elle ne peut être résorbée.

Le rôle de directeur·trice de l’architecture logicielle existe pour combler cet écart. Il s’agit d’un poste de leadership technique pratique et hautement spécialisé, chargé de définir et d’appliquer les normes d’architecture d’entreprise à l’échelle de l’organisation Produits et Technologie de Power Factors (couvrant les secteurs Plateforme, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps et CAM/FSM/Ops produit), tout en concevant et en prototypant personnellement les problèmes les plus complexes auxquels l’organisation est confrontée, notamment en matière d’introduction de produits basés sur l’IA, d’acquisition de données IoT et d’évolutivité SaaS multitenant.

Ce poste combine la portée stratégique d’un·e architecte d’entreprise et la crédibilité d’un·e bâtisseur·euse qui continue d’écrire du code, de réviser des demandes de tirage (pull requests) et d’être à l’aise en tant que personne la plus technique dans la salle.

Relevant directement du ou de la Chef·fe des produits et de la technologie (CPTO), la personne titulaire agit comme tissu connectif entre la stratégie organisationnelle du ou de la CPTO et les décisions techniques quotidiennes prises par les équipes d’ingénierie verticales, en collaborant étroitement avec les responsables des secteurs (Plateforme, SCADA, EMS, APM, CloudOps, CAM/FSM/Ops produit), la gestion de produit et les équipes CloudOps et Sécurité.

Il est important de noter que ce rôle n’est pas un poste purement stratégique ou consultatif éloigné du code, ni un rôle de gestion axé sur les processus et les rapports. La personne titulaire est appelée à demeurer un·e contributeur·trice technique crédible et actif·ve tout au long de son mandat. Ce poste ne comprend pas non plus la responsabilité de la priorisation de la feuille de route produit ou de la stratégie commerciale, car ces responsabilités demeurent avec la gestion de produit et le ou la CPTO. Il façonne toutefois directement ce qui est techniquement possible et à quelle vitesse cela peut être livré.
