jobs.title: VP of Product
jobs.text:
About Leena AI
Leena AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Colleagues don't just answer employee questions — they run the work behind them: case handling, approvals and transactions across systems like Workday, SAP SuccessFactors and ServiceNow.
We compete — and win — against ServiceNow + Moveworks, Workday Illuminate and vertical point solutions. We do it with vendor-agnostic, cross-functional orchestration, the broadest connector coverage in the category, and deployments measured in weeks, not quarters.
The business is working: ARR has passed $20M and tripled in the last 12 months. Gartner has named us a Leader in agentic AI three times running, and hundreds of enterprises — including Nestlé and Coca-Cola — run on Leena AI. We're headquartered in New York, with our product and engineering hub in Gurugram.
The role
We're hiring a VP of Product to own what Leena AI builds, why, and how we know it worked. You'll report to Adit Jain, our co-founder and CEO, and lead the product org across our pods — knowledge management, AI Colleague Studio, integrations, and the HR, IT and Finance agents.
We've built the platform. The next stage is harder: turning a strong agentic platform into the system of record for back-office work, while competing against incumbents who own the underlying systems. That takes a product leader who can set a sharp strategy, decompose it into metrics, and carry senior rooms — internally and with Fortune 500 CIOs and CHROs.
This is not a roadmap-routing role. We want someone who decides, holds a line under pressure, and builds a product org that does the same.
What you own
Product strategy and vision. Define where Leena AI wins over the next 24 months — which back-office workflows we go deep on across HR, IT, Finance and Legal, and where we stay horizontal. Turn that into a multi-quarter roadmap the company can bet on.
The metric tree. Own a clear north star (e.g., autonomous resolution rate, or work completed end-to-end without a human) and the decomposed tree of input metrics beneath it, with owners and quarterly movement targets for every pod. If a pod's plan is a list of features rather than a model of its metric, send it back.
The agentic platform. Set direction for AI Colleague Studio, our agent orchestration layer, voice, and the knowledge layer — so customers' builders can design, test, govern and deploy agents themselves without raising a ticket with us.
Integrations as a moat. Keep our connector breadth and depth ahead of the market — Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, ServiceNow, Oracle, ADP, Salesforce and Microsoft 365 — and make sure agents land transactions correctly across them.
Enterprise trust. Make data residency, audit trails, explainability, permissions and agent guardrails first-class product features, not RFP afterthoughts.
Field to product loop. Partner with Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions and our HR domain leads so what we learn in each implementation ships to the next customer by default. Cut time-to-value release over release.
Go-to-market alignment. Work with Sales, Product Marketing and Demand Gen on positioning, packaging and pricing. Be in the room for strategic deals, QBRs, customer advisory boards and analyst briefings.
Team. Lead and grow a team of product managers and designers across New York and Gurugram. Raise the bar on PRDs, metric thinking and customer presence. Hire well and fast as we scale.
Operating cadence. Run planning, roadmap reviews and launch readiness with Engineering, Design, CS and Sales on a single prioritized backlog.

jobs.title: Director of Business Technology & AI
jobs.text:
Proactive Technology Management is partnering with Michigan Planners, an established employee benefits and retirement services organization, to identify an experienced and forward-thinking Director of Business Technology & AI.
MI Planners is seeking a technology leader who can bring a fresh perspective to their organization, identify opportunities for improvement, and help transform the way they operate through AI, Salesforce optimization, and strategic technology initiatives.
Location
We are looking for someone to work full time in or around either Washington, MI or Traverse City, MI. You'd be expected to be on-site at least 2-3 days out of the week.
About the Role
We are seeking an innovative, hands-on technology leader who enjoys solving problems, challenging existing processes, and identifying opportunities to make businesses more efficient.
The primary focus of this position will be evaluating and implementing AI solutions, optimizing Salesforce, and overseeing internal technology operations.
This is not a traditional IT Director position focused solely on maintaining existing systems. The ideal candidate will bring a consultative mindset, take the time to understand how the business operates, and identify opportunities to improve processes through technology.
Success in this role requires a combination of technical expertise, analytical thinking, and the ability to turn ideas into practical solutions. Experience within the health insurance or employee benefits industry, particularly in environments subject to HIPAA regulations, is highly desirable.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
About CarbonChain
The fight against Climate Change is evolving rapidly. Climate tech is changing. The first wave was reporting. The next is treating carbon the way companies treat money: as a way to decide what to buy, who to sell to, and which incentives to claim.
Around the world, carbon is becoming a condition of trade. Border taxes, free allocations, green premiums, cheaper capital. It looks a lot like the post-war rebuild: governments put capital and tax incentives on the table, and the companies that could keep the books moved first. The missing piece then was bookkeeping. The missing piece now is the same, carbon accounting.
CarbonChain is that bookkeeping. We turn messy, real-world supply-chain data into numbers a trader, a sustainability lead, or a CFO will actually use.
We want people who are agents of change, who feel the impact of climate change and know there is no way around it to create a better future for every being.
People who know the customer is the truth of how a company thrives. People who treat data as the fuel for how fast society can change. People who use AI to accelerate the cause for good by working through an AI lens first to automate repetitive tasks and analyse data. Finally, people who enjoy working with people.
Our Product
We help the world's largest commodity producers and traders measure and cut emissions, with verified primary data where we can get it and defensible defaults where we cannot. The platform turns operational and supplier files into decision-grade carbon and compliance insight: sourcing, CBAM, product and corporate footprints, reporting customers and regulators will stand behind.
We organise carbon accounting around the user in four contexts at once:
Immediate: the tools in front of them
Internal: how they work with colleagues
External: how they work with suppliers and customers
Societal: how they work with society, governments, and disclosing bodies
The data we hold is only useful if it makes all four of those jobs easier.
Head of Product
About the Role
We’re looking for a Head of Product to own and shape the product function at CarbonChain. Working closely with our founders and senior leadership, you’ll set the product strategy and roadmap, decide what we build and why, and build a product team and culture that consistently delivers real value to our customers.
You’ll sit at the heart of the business alongside Customer Success, Sales, Engineering, and our Carbon Advisory Team. Your job is to balance internal insight with knowledge gathered directly from customers and the wider market to work out which customer problems are worth solving and how, combining those inputs with product data and your own discovery, and turn that into a clear, evidence-based roadmap that balances quick wins that unblock customers today against the bigger bets that will set us apart tomorrow.
This role calls for an outstanding product leader who can get to grips with a complex domain quickly. You will need to think deeply about the customer value proposition in a decarbonising world; and the 10 year + view of ESG software in a volatile political horizon. Our customers are some of the world’s largest commodities producers and traders, facing fast-moving regulation and growing pressure for credible emissions reporting. You’ll need to understand their world deeply, anticipate where it’s heading, and make sure CarbonChain is always one step ahead. Much of the value customers get today comes from our expert carbon advisory service combined with product capabilities. You’ll need to think about how product intelligence can scale on the foundations of rapidly advancing AI models.
What You’ll Do
Own the product function end to end, maturing our product capability and establishing a consistent methodology for how we discover, scope, prioritise, and deliver
Work with the founders and senior leadership to define the product vision, strategy, and roadmap, and translate them into clear plans the whole business can rally behind
Partner closely with Customer Success, Sales, Engineering, and the Carbon Team to understand customer problems and assess requests against evidence, building a roadmap that balances rapid releases against longer-term strategic investments
Raise the quality of how we scope and deliver, working with our Carbon Advisory Team’s deep industry expertise so that what we build is methodologically sound, auditable, and genuinely useful
Stay close to the climate tech market, regulatory developments, and our customers’ challenges, working with Sales and Customer Success to evolve our products ahead of upcoming societal sentiment, executive’s priorities and competitive shifts
Set a high bar for evidence-based decision-making, challenging assumptions constructively wherever they come from, whether that’s inside the business or from our largest customers. Be highly truth seeking.
Build a strong product culture: hire, coach, and develop product managers and UX/UI designers into a confident, engaged, high-performing team
Act as the product champion across the business, protecting the mission, communicating priorities and trade-offs clearly while protecting the team’s time and space to do deep, creative work
Converting difficult conversations with customers and complex subject matter into collaborative problem-solving projects in partnership with customers to drive solutions and create tangible commercial value.
Define how we measure product success, tracking adoption, outcomes, and impact well after launch and feeding what we learn back into the roadmap
What We’re Looking For
Extensive experience in product management, including experience in leading product teams or a product function, ideally in a scaling B2B SaaS company
Experience building data-intensive products where data quality, provenance, or auditability matter, in the face of customer demands for simplicity and an improved user interface
The curiosity and rigour to get to depth quickly in a technical, regulated domain, and to hold your own on methodology with our Carbon Advisory Team within your first few months
A track record of defining and delivering product strategy that drove measurable customer adoption and business growth
Experience running user acceptance testing with real customers and embracing customer feedback as an input to tightening product-market-fit
Experience establishing or maturing product processes, from discovery and prioritisation frameworks to roadmapping and release planning
Hands-on discovery practice: you’ve personally run customer research and prototype tests, and know how to de-risk a bet before committing engineering to it
A rigorous, evidence-led approach to decision-making, and the confidence to challenge assumptions at every level
Proven ability to hire, coach, and develop product managers and designers, and to build a healthy product culture
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including handling complex, technical, or contentious topics with senior internal stakeholders and enterprise customers
Strong collaboration skills: you work closely with Engineering to understand technical trade-offs, and with commercial teams to keep the roadmap grounded in real customer needs
Comfortable with ambiguity and changing priorities, and pragmatic about shipping MVPs to learn quickly from real users
Bonus: knowledge of carbon accounting and the wider climate and regulatory or sustainability landscape, such as GHG Protocol, product carbon footprinting, Scope 3, or CBAM
Bonus: familiarity with commodities, manufacturing, or heavy industry supply chains
How We Work
As a hybrid co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the UK and US. This role would be located 3d/week in our London LABS Camden office space. You will need the right to work in the UK.
What We Offer
Meaningful impact and accelerated growth.
This is a rare opportunity to work on technology that directly addresses the climate crisis while shaping the future of a fast-growing company. You'll work closely with leadership to define product direction.
You'll tackle diverse challenges, work across the full stack of problems (technical and societal), and own meaningful projects from start to finish. If you want to learn quickly, take on real responsibility, and see the direct results of your work, this is the place to do it.
Competitive salary and benefits:
28 days annual leave
£500 home office setup allowance
£2,000 annual learning allowance
Private healthcare
Company pension incl. salary sacrifice options
Generous parental leave policy
Weekly team lunches in the office
Office gym, and cycle to work scheme
Remote work contribution of £1,000 towards expenses for 1-week abroad
Equal Opportunity Employer
CarbonChain is dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and supportive work environment that brings people together from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all.
If you think your skills and experience match what we're looking for and you'd like to join next Climate Tech adventure, please get in touch.
You can find out more about interviewing at CarbonChain at carbonchain.com/careers/interview-process.
CarbonChain values diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds.
If you think your skills and experience match what we’re looking for and you’d like to join the next Climate Tech industry unicorn, please get in touch!
You can find out more about interviewing at CarbonChain at https://www.carbonchain.com/careers/interview-process.

jobs.title: AI & Data Senior Vice President - APAC
jobs.text:
At AlixPartners, we solve the most complex and critical challenges by moving quickly from analysis to action when it really matters, creating value that has a lasting impact on companies, their people, and the communities they serve.
By understanding, respecting and supporting the needs of our employees, clients and communities, AlixPartners fosters an inclusive environment where authenticity, growth and collaboration thrive. We believe diversity strengthens our perspectives, improves our decisions and ultimately delivers better outcomes for our clients.
What you’ll do
As a Senior Vice President in our APAC AI Transformation team, you will lead complex AI workstreams and engagements, guide multidisciplinary teams and help senior clients move from AI ambition to scaled implementation and measurable value.
Your responsibilities will include:
AI Strategy & Transformation
Shape enterprise AI strategies, investment priorities and implementation roadmaps.
Identify and prioritize high-value AI opportunities across functions, industries and APAC markets.
Design AI-enabled operating models, governance structures and transformation programmes.
Advise senior executives on AI investment, risk, governance, adoption and value realization.
Lead organisational change and implementation planning for enterprise AI transformation.
Build & Prototype
Lead teams building Proofs of Concept and Minimum Viable Products using APIs from leading Large Language Models.
Guide the development and deployment of AI agents in enterprise environments, including system integration, orchestration, monitoring and controls.
Oversee Retrieval-Augmented Generation and knowledge solutions using vector databases and secure enterprise data.
Set design principles for intelligent workflows, automation, responsible AI and security.
Translate complex business challenges into scalable AI solutions and delivery programmes.
Deliver Business Impact
Lead AI solution delivery alongside client executives, business owners and technical teams.
Drive enterprise adoption, change management and capability transfer.
Define and track business outcomes, value realization and solution performance.
Resolve trade-offs between business priorities, technical feasibility, risk and time to value.
Ensure solutions are responsible, secure, scalable and aligned with enterprise objectives.
Build the Practice
As our APAC AI Transformation capabilities grow, you will also contribute to:
developing differentiated client offerings and sector-specific AI propositions;
creating reusable methodologies, accelerators and intellectual property;
leading proposal development and supporting business development;
managing and mentoring teams of consultants and technical specialists;
strengthening AlixPartners' market leadership in AI Transformation across APAC.
This description is not intended to provide an exhaustive list of responsibilities.
What you’ll need
Your Profile
We are looking for an experienced AI transformation leader who combines consulting judgement, hands-on technical credibility and strong delivery leadership.
The successful candidate will be comfortable leading engagements, managing senior stakeholders and coaching teams across multiple APAC markets.
Relevant backgrounds may include leading IT consulting firms, commercial AI solution teams within technology companies, specialised AI firms, or senior corporate technology, digital, product and AI teams.
Successful candidates will typically demonstrate:
about 10-14 years of working experience with outstanding structured problem-solving, programme leadership and commercial judgement;
hands-on professional experience building Generative AI solutions using LLM APIs; hands-on professional experience and deep credibility in Generative AI solutions, Machine Learning, Data Modelling/analysis
experience leading the development and deployment of enterprise AI agents;
a strong record of moving AI solutions from prototype to production and adoption;
excellent executive communication, stakeholder management and team leadership skills;
the ability to bridge strategy, operations, data and technology;
an entrepreneurial mindset, ownership and the ability to lead through ambiguity.
Technical Experience
The following capabilities are essential:
Hands-on experience building enterprise GenAI solutions using LLM APIs, MLOps, cloud architectures etc. training or self-learning alone is not sufficient.
Experience leading the development and deployment of AI agents in enterprise environments, including integration, orchestration, monitoring and controls.
Demonstrated experience leading AI solutions from prototype or proof of concept into production at scale.
Experience developing or commercializing AI products, AI-enabled devices or robotics is advantageous.
Experience with RAG, vector databases, AI governance, responsible AI and security is advantageous.
Technical credibility must be based on real professional delivery and deployment, not solely training, certification or personal experimentation.
Consulting experience is a plus, but is not required where the candidate has strong enterprise AI leadership, commercialization and stakeholder experience.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English
Willingness to work outside of normal business hours, and in particular as unique projects/needs arise.
Ability to work full time in an office and remote environment; physically able to sit/stand at a computer and work in front of a computer screen for significant portions of the workday
Must become familiar with, and promote and abide by, our Core Values as defined by the AlixPartners’ Code of Conduct and foster an inclusive environment with people at all levels of an organisation
The firm offers market-leading benefits that provide flexible options to support our employee’s needs including health benefits to help prioritise their physical and emotional well-being, time-off policies to help to recharge and financial/ retirement benefits that offer income protection and support long-term planning.
The benefit type and level differ per location.
AlixPartners is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, among other things, race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, status as a protected veteran, or disability.

jobs.text:
At AlixPartners, we solve the most complex and critical challenges by moving quickly from analysis to action when it really matters, creating value that has a lasting impact on companies, their people, and the communities they serve.
By understanding, respecting and supporting the needs of our employees, clients and communities, AlixPartners fosters an inclusive environment where authenticity, growth and collaboration thrive. We believe diversity strengthens our perspectives, improves our decisions and ultimately delivers better outcomes for our clients.
What you’ll do
AI Transformation
Artificial Intelligence is creating one of the largest business transformations of our generation. While many organizations are experimenting with AI, relatively few have succeeded in turning it into measurable business value.
At AlixPartners, we help clients move beyond experimentation.
We combine strategy, transformation and execution to help organization's identify high-impact AI opportunities, redesign operating models, prototype solutions, deploy AI at scale and create sustainable business outcomes.
Our AI Transformation team brings together experienced consultants, AI specialists and industry experts to help organizations rethink how they operate, make decisions and create value. Working with colleagues across our global network, we support clients across APAC in functions including operations, finance, procurement, supply chain, commercial excellence and corporate strategy.
Our ambition is to build a team of consultants who combine outstanding business judgement with modern AI capabilities.
This is a unique opportunity to help shape our AI Transformation capabilities across APAC and influence how AI consulting evolves within AlixPartners.
What We Offer
Impactful, hands-on and pragmatic—at AlixPartners, your career is driven by performance, initiative and the value you create.
Working in small, highly experienced teams, you will collaborate directly with CEOs, executive committees, Boards and private equity investors on some of their most strategic and time-critical challenges.
Our consultants do more than develop recommendations. They work alongside clients to design solutions, prototype rapidly, deploy at scale and measure the impact created.
One week you may be helping a CEO define an enterprise AI strategy. The next, you may be building an AI-enabled solution to automate a critical business process, improve decision-making or transform the way an organization operates.
This unique combination of strategy, execution and technology is what differentiates AlixPartners.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Design
jobs.text:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.
As the Senior Director of Design, Governance & Compliance at Vanta, you'll lead design for our largest product pillar. You'll set the direction for how compliance work moves from manual workflows to agents that do the work alongside our customers.
Governance & Compliance is the core of Vanta. It covers the frameworks, controls, policies, audits, and org structures that thousands of companies use to run their security programs. Those companies range from founders getting their first SOC2 to global enterprises managing hundreds of controls. As we move upmarket, the team's job is to make that complexity feel simple for every customer, at every size.
You’ll lead a team of senior, staff, and principal designers, with senior managers and directors reporting to you. You'll report to the Head of Design and partner as a peer with product and engineering leadership for the pillar. We're not starting from scratch. Vanta Agent works across the product, customers build and deploy their own custom agents, and our designers prototype and ship to production with our own AI design harness. Your job is to make that the way the whole pillar works.
What you’ll do as a Senior Director of Design at Vanta:
Lead the agentic direction for Governance & Compliance. Build on the agents we've already shipped, define what comes next, and shape how people and agents work together across the pillar
Own design quality across the pillar. Set the bar, drive consistency from concept to ship, and get into the details yourself when it matters
Design for platform and enterprise complexity. Lead the team through cross-cutting decisions on scoping, segmentation, org units, permissions, and multi-entity audits so the system holds together across surfaces
Bring AI into how the team works. Build on our design harness, help every designer prototype and ship faster, and keep craft high as speed goes up
Lead and grow leaders. Develop your design leaders and senior ICs, build a high-trust team, and hire well as the pillar grows
Partner as a peer with product and engineering. Co-own outcomes and quality with your counterparts, not just the design work
How to be successful in this role:
You've shipped agentic or AI-forward products and have a point of view on how design changes when outputs are non-deterministic
You use AI hands-on in your own process, from prototyping to building in a harness or in code, and you bring your team along
You have deep enterprise B2B SaaS experience. You understand custom configurations, multi-org workflows, and large deployments, and you've made complex products feel simple
You think in systems, designing object models and patterns that hold up across many surfaces, not just individual flows
You're comfortable going deep with engineers in a technical, domain-heavy space like GRC
You've led teams of 12 or more, including design directors, design managers, and staff ICs, and you move easily between strategy and the details
You have a portfolio showing how you've simplified complex products and shipped AI-forward experiences (required for interview)
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship
Responsible for protecting Vanta and customer data in how your team operates and delivers results
Use AI in day-to-day work to amplify your skills and strengthen your outcomes, applying it across routine workflows, actively building fluency through experimentation, and exercising sound judgment to ensure AI-assisted work meets a high quality bar
What you can expect as a Vanta’n:
Industry-competitive salary and equity
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans
16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents
Health & wellness stipend
Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend
Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office
Family planning benefits
Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting
Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time
11 company-paid holidays
Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!
Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney
To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.
#LI-remote
At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.
About Vanta
We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged.
Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.
Referral Instructions
If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

What you’ll do as a Senior Director of Design at Vanta:
Lead the agentic direction for Governance & Compliance. Build on the agents we've already shipped, define what comes next, and shape how people and agents work together across the pillar
Own design quality across the pillar. Set the bar, drive consistency from concept to ship, and get into the details yourself when it matters

Design for platform and enterprise complexity. Lead the team through cross-cutting decisions on scoping, segmentation, org units, permissions, and multi-entity audits so the system holds together across surfaces
Bring AI into how the team works. Build on our design harness, help every designer prototype and ship faster, and keep craft high as speed goes up
Lead and grow leaders. Develop your design leaders and senior ICs, build a high-trust team, and hire well as the pillar grows
Partner as a peer with product and engineering. Co-own outcomes and quality with your counterparts, not just the design work
How to be successful in this role:
You've shipped agentic or AI-forward products and have a point of view on how design changes when outputs are non-deterministic
You use AI hands-on in your own process, from prototyping to building in a harness or in code, and you bring your team along
You have deep enterprise B2B SaaS experience. You understand custom configurations, multi-org workflows, and large deployments, and you've made complex products feel simple
You think in systems, designing object models and patterns that hold up across many surfaces, not just individual flows
You're comfortable going deep with engineers in a technical, domain-heavy space like GRC
You've led teams of 12 or more, including design directors, design managers, and staff ICs, and you move easily between strategy and the details
You have a portfolio showing how you've simplified complex products and shipped AI-forward experiences (required for interview)
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship
Responsible for protecting Vanta and customer data in how your team operates and delivers results

Use AI in day-to-day work to amplify your skills and strengthen your outcomes, applying it across routine workflows, actively building fluency through experimentation, and exercising sound judgment to ensure AI-assisted work meets a high quality bar
What you can expect as a Vanta’n:
Industry-competitive salary and equity
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee-only benefit premiums covered for most medical plans
16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents
Health & wellness stipend
Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend
Commuter benefits for team members who report to the SF and NYC office
Family planning benefits
Matching 401(k) contribution with immediate vesting
Flexible PTO policy, plus 80 hours of Sick Time
11 company-paid holidays
Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!
Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney

To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. We set standard base pay ranges for all roles based on function, level, and country location, benchmarked against similar-stage growth companies. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.
#LI-remote

At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.
About Vanta

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged.

Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

jobs.title: VP of HubSpot & Technology Services
jobs.text:
Hybrid (Cheshire, CT area preferred). Occasional travel 1–2 times per quarter.
New role: one of four leadership positions we’re adding to support IMPACT’s next phase of growth. Open to internal and external candidates.
We're looking for a leader to build and run IMPACT's HubSpot and Technology practice for the next several years, so clients' sales and marketing teams adopt their platforms and use them to grow. You'll own IMPACT's HubSpot partnership day to day and help decide which platforms we train on next.
You'll be building on a strong foundation. Our HubSpot partnership matters a lot to the business, and today much of our work comes through referrals from our Endless Customers coaching clients. Now we need you to grow the practice on its own strength. That means building new sources of demand by making the most of the HubSpot partnership and expanding into other technologies.
We’re looking for someone who can take the goals for this practice, build a plan they believe in, and lead the team through it. You’ll set the priorities and make the day-to-day calls. If results are off pace or an offering isn’t delivering for clients, you’ll spot it early, decide what needs to change, and follow through without waiting for direction.
The job is to deliver the 2027 results and build a practice that you and your team can keep growing profitably into 2028 and beyond.
About IMPACT
IMPACT helps businesses become the most recommended, trusted, and chosen company in their market with the Endless Customers System (formerly They Ask, You Answer). We coach companies to earn buyer trust through content, video, sales alignment, their website, and visibility in AI search, and we're also a HubSpot Diamond Partner. We offer additional services such as website redesign, and paid media management.
We typically work with businesses in the range of $5-100m in revenue, often in home services, manufacturing, retail, and professional services. Most of the time, the business owner decides whether to engage with us, and sometimes it's the head of marketing or sales.
Room to shape the practice
You'll have room to shape the practice around your vision for what buyers will need in 2027 and beyond. Within certain parameters, you'll decide which services to develop, what to charge, and how your team delivers them profitably. We're counting on you to build a team that works well together and produces results clients can point to when they tell the story of what IMPACT did for their business.
Make the tools work for the people
Platforms keep getting more powerful, and AI is changing what they can do every month. Most teams can't keep up. You'll help clients own and run their own systems. You'll never lock them in or add complexity they don't need, and you'll keep our training current as HubSpot and other tools change.
What you'll do
Grow a profitable practice
Own the practice's revenue and profitability
Follow up quickly on opportunities from Marketing & Sales and our coaches, and scope and close custom and expanded engagements.
Keep forecasts current
Spot at-risk clients early and lead documented recovery plans.
Recommend renewals and expansions only when there's a clear next outcome for the client.
Deliver consistently at scale
Certify trainers on the platforms they teach, and review training quality regularly.
Keep materials current as HubSpot and other tools release new features.
Coordinate training scope and sequencing with our Web, Paid Media and coaching teams, so shared client processes aren't redesigned in isolation.
Own the HubSpot partnership
Track partner-tier requirements, with a dated plan to close any gaps and reach Elite status.
Keep deal registration and team certifications current.
Turn HubSpot referrals, co-marketing and partner-program opportunities into pipeline.
Grow our tier through work that fits the client and is profitable, never by selling unnecessary licenses.
Evolve the products
Shape our training lineup around market demand, client feedback and what the team enjoys delivering.
Evaluate new platforms, such as other CRMs and Notion
Fix or retire offers that don't sell or don't deliver, and recommend new offers and pricing changes
Work as One IMPACT
Coordinate cross-practice handoffs through each client's Relationship Owner.
Contribute expert time to marketing and sales (content, events and sales conversations) and to the Endless Customers Academy.
Test AI and process improvements, and share what works with the other practices.
Lead the team
Lead, develop and hold the team accountable, with clear expectations, measurables and regular feedback.
Make sure the team has the skills, tools, certifications and documentation it needs.
Who you'll work with
You'll report to our Integrator and work closely with our Visionary, who owns the executive-level HubSpot relationship. You'll also partner with the VPs of EC Coaching & Training, Web Services and Paid Media Services on shared clients, and with Marketing & Sales on new business.

jobs.title: Head of Platform & Infrastructure Engineering
jobs.text:
Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future.
We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!
The Role
In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:
Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.
Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).
Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!
Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.
Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.
You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.
If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!
A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!
The Qualifications
We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:
You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.
You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.
You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.
You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.
You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.
You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.
You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.
What We’re Building
As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.
Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.
As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!
Why You Shouldn’t Apply
You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.
You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.
You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).
You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.
To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.
You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.
Engineering Culture
Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:
Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design
Natural collaboration and deliberate communication
Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.
Putting effort into building a diverse team
Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership
The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.
Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”
At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.
Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate
Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).
To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:
We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.
Increase Leverage, not Team Size
We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:
Great developer tooling. For example, our CI/CD takes ~10m, we deploy at least 15x a day, and our debugger works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.
Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).
AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.
Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:
And a demo of one of these building blocks:
Put Effort into Diversity
Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.
Today, 30% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We actively maintain and improve these numbers by sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, banning leetcode interviews, providing guidance and coaching to candidates, and more.
Work-Life Balance: It’s A Marathon, Not a Sprint
The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.
Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives engineers (and to a similar degree, you) a lot of flexibility in how they structure their days and weeks. In practice, that means they keep their own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching their feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and they actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.
This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school. Mujda (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”
Interview Process
This is an important role that will lead our Platform & Infrastructure teams now and for the foreseeable future. The interview process reflects that in both challenge and length (5 rounds, ~6.5h):
Introduction call with me (30m, live)
A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)
An interview to explore your past experience as a leader (1h, live)
Interview with Colin, our Head of EMEA Engineering (45m)
Final round where you meet various folks on the team and explore leadership and technical topics (3h)
I’ll have a strong read on whether we’re trending toward an offer by Round 3. Near the end of the process, we’ll do reference checks with a former manager, two direct reports, and a peer in Engineering. Depending on my bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.
This is also an important decision for you, so once you start interviewing, I’m always happy to have coffee chats in person or over Zoom to get to know each other.
Your First Six Months at Ashby
Your first three months at Ashby will be spent learning about Ashby Engineering and easing into leadership. While most of your onboarding will be driven by a 6-month plan you put together (and refine over time), you’ll also ship some product changes, features, and infra changes. What better way to learn how ICs work than to be one! Don’t worry if you’re not familiar with our technologies. The team is really helpful, and our dev environment is pretty awesome: it sets up in a single script, and you’ll be able to push your first product change on day one.
You and I will do 30-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 6-month reviews to calibrate on our unique culture and how you, I, and the team will work together.
Benefits
Competitive salary and equity.
10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.
Unlimited PTO.
A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.
Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!
$100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.
If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.
Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.
Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.
Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!
The Qualifications
We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.
You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.

You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.

You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.

You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.

You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.
What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!
Why You Shouldn’t Apply
You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.

You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.
You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.
Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:
Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design
Natural collaboration and deliberate communication
Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.
Putting effort into building a diverse team
Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.
Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).
To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:
We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.
Increase Leverage, not Team Size
We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:
Great developer tooling. For example, our CI/CD takes ~10m, we deploy at least 15x a day, and our debugger works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.
Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:
And a demo of one of these building blocks:
Put Effort into Diversity

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 30% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We actively maintain and improve these numbers by sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, banning leetcode interviews, providing guidance and coaching to candidates, and more.
Work-Life Balance: It’s A Marathon, Not a Sprint

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives engineers (and to a similar degree, you) a lot of flexibility in how they structure their days and weeks. In practice, that means they keep their own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching their feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and they actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school. Mujda (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”
Interview Process
This is an important role that will lead our Platform & Infrastructure teams now and for the foreseeable future. The interview process reflects that in both challenge and length (5 rounds, ~6.5h):
Introduction call with me (30m, live)
A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)
An interview to explore your past experience as a leader (1h, live)
Interview with Colin, our Head of EMEA Engineering (45m)
Final round where you meet various folks on the team and explore leadership and technical topics (3h)

I’ll have a strong read on whether we’re trending toward an offer by Round 3. Near the end of the process, we’ll do reference checks with a former manager, two direct reports, and a peer in Engineering. Depending on my bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.
This is also an important decision for you, so once you start interviewing, I’m always happy to have coffee chats in person or over Zoom to get to know each other.
Your First Six Months at Ashby

Your first three months at Ashby will be spent learning about Ashby Engineering and easing into leadership. While most of your onboarding will be driven by a 6-month plan you put together (and refine over time), you’ll also ship some product changes, features, and infra changes. What better way to learn how ICs work than to be one! Don’t worry if you’re not familiar with our technologies. The team is really helpful, and our dev environment is pretty awesome: it sets up in a single script, and you’ll be able to push your first product change on day one.
You and I will do 30-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 6-month reviews to calibrate on our unique culture and how you, I, and the team will work together.
Benefits
Competitive salary and equity.
10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.
Unlimited PTO.
A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.
Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!
$100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management (Consumer)
jobs.text:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
About the Product team
The Product team listens to our customers’ needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision.
About the role
Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without hidden fees or compounding interest. Our Direct to Consumer Products, Surfaces, and Growth programs are a fast-growing product set that operates with the agility of a startup while leveraging the scale of an industry leader, delivering quality Consumer Experiences to our Consumers and Growth to the business alike.
You will be a pivotal strategic leader responsible for defining the next chapter of Affirm's Consumer & Card Growth programs. You will lead a portfolio of high-impact consumer journeys that directly influence conversion, engagement, and revenue. This is a role for a seasoned product leader obsessed with consumer experiences and quality, driving Consumer Product growth ie Cards, and disrupting the payments & credit landscape
What you'll do
Strategic Leadership: Define and socialize a long-term Growth and App vision and strategy, and translate that vision into clear roadmaps and decisions that teams can execute against
Portfolio Oversight: Manage and scale a portfolio of consumer-facing surfaces, and growth platforms, including Onboarding flows, App surfaces, and platforms like Segmentation & Targeting services, ensuring a simple and consistent experience across platforms
Lead and grow a high-performing PM team. Build, mentor, and manage a team of product managers, including people managers. You'll set the bar for craft, create development paths, and cultivate a culture of ownership, rigor, and candor.
Executive Communication: Proactively align senior leadership on strategy, execution risks, and mitigation plans, ensuring organizational clarity during complex initiatives
Drive cross-functional alignment at scale: Partner with Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Revenue leaders to optimize the marketplace ecosystem, balancing merchant value with consumer experiences
Operational Excellence: Establish frameworks for rigorous experimentation and funnel analysis to drive measurable gains in completion rates and customer retention
What we look for
Experience: 10+ years of product management leadership, with a proven track record of shipping large-scale consumer products in fintech, e-commerce, or marketplace environments.
Strategic Clarity: Demonstrated ability to bring "clarity when things feel messy," turning ambiguous problems into crisp narratives and structured execution plans.
AI/LLM Fluency: Familiarity with AI-native product development, including agentic patterns and LLM-powered discovery experiences, to lead our highest-leverage bets in search
Analytical Rigor: Exceptional ability to use data (including LTV/CAC and profitability assessments) to guide prioritization and quantify the impact of product features.
People Leadership: Experience operating through layers of leadership, delegating ownership effectively, and scaling decision-making across diverse product lines.
Consumer Empathy: A "consumer-first" mindset with a high bar for design polish and a commitment to delivering honest financial products
Pay Grade - T
Equity Grade - USA 18
Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.
Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)
USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $300,000 - $360,000
USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $267,000 - $327,000
#LI-Remote
Remote-first with flexibility built in
Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.
Benefits designed for you
Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:
Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.
We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.
For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.
By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's Global Candidate Privacy Notice and consent to the use of your personal information as described.

jobs.text: The Vice President of Technology leads WorldVia's technology organization including software engineering, travel technology, IT and network infrastructure, information security, and AI workflow automation. Reporting to the CEO, this role turns WorldVia's technology direction and product roadmap into working systems, and owns how the technology team is built, how work is delivered, and how systems run day to day. The VP manages the software engineering team directly while building out the organization and is accountable for the systems that independent travel advisors and WorldVia staff rely on, including WorldVia's One platform, worldvia.com, advisor booking tools, travel-system integrations, and various third-party systems.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Forward Deployed Engineering - REMOTE (Plano, TX, US)
jobs.text:
NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.
We are currently seeking a Managing Director, Forward Deployed Engineering - REMOTE to join our team in Plano, Texas (US-TX), United States (US).
Position Summary
NTT DATA is building a new Forward Deployed Engineering capability to accelerate AI Service-as-Software, one of the company's key strategic growth bets. We are seeking an Executive, Head of Forward Deployed Engineering to build and lead this function globally.
